exam_questions.question_text:
Which combination represents all possible sets of quantum numbers for the $3d$ electrons?

$$

| \text{Choices} | n | l | m_l | m_s |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| \text{A} | 3 | 2 | -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 | \pm 1/2 |
| \text{B} | 3 | 1 | -1, 0, 1 | \pm 1/2 |
| \text{C} | 3 | 2 | -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3 | +1/2 |
| \text{D} | 3 | 1 | -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 | \pm 1/2 |

$$
exam_questions.explanation: For the $3d$ subshell, the principal quantum number $n = 3$, orbital angular momentum quantum number for a $d$-orbital is $l = 2$, magnetic quantum number $m_l$ ranges from $-l$ to $+l$ ($-2, -1, 0, +1, +2$), and spin quantum number $m_s = \pm 1/2$.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following sets shows the correct first four members of the alkane series?
exam_questions.option_a: Methane, Ethene, Propane, Butane
exam_questions.option_b: Methane, Methanol, Ethanol, Butanol
exam_questions.option_c: Methane, Ethyne, Propane, Butene
exam_questions.explanation: The homologous series of unbranched alkanes ($C_n H_{2n+2}$) begins with Methane ($CH_4$), Ethane ($C_2H_6$), Propane ($C_3H_8$), and Butane ($C_4H_{10}$).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: Given elements: $\text{O}, \text{Be}, \text{N}, \text{B}, \text{F}$: which is the correct increasing order of first ionization energy?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{Be} < \text{B} < \text{N} < \text{O} < \text{F}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{F} < \text{B} < \text{Be} < \text{O} < \text{N}$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{N} < \text{B} < \text{O} < \text{Be} < \text{F}$
exam_questions.explanation: Across Period 2, ionization energy increases generally, with standard anomalies: $\text{B} (2s^2 2p^1) < \text{Be} (2s^2)$ due to shielding by the full $2s$ subshell, and $\text{O} (2s^2 2p^4) < \text{N} (2s^2 2p^3)$ due to spin-pairing repulsion in oxygen's $2p$ orbital vs Nitrogen's stable half-filled subshell. Thus, the order is $\text{B} < \text{Be} < \text{O} < \text{N} < \text{F}$.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding the formation of ionic compounds?
exam_questions.option_a: Ionic compounds are formed when electrons are shared between atoms.
exam_questions.option_b: Ionic compounds are formed between atoms with similar electronegativity.
exam_questions.option_c: Ionic compounds form when electrons transfer red from one atom to another.
exam_questions.option_d: Ionic compounds formed by delocalization of electrons in metal.
exam_questions.explanation: Ionic bonds are electrostatic attractions formed when one or more valence electrons are completely transfer red from an electropositive metallic atom to an electronegative non-metallic atom.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: Why is graphite a good conductor of electricity, while diamond ($\text{C}$) is not, even though both are forms of carbon allotropes?
exam_questions.option_a: Graphite has delocalized electrons due to its hexagonal structure, while diamond does not
exam_questions.option_b: Graphite is a metal having delocalized electron while diamond is a non-metal doesn’t.
exam_questions.option_c: Diamond has metallic bonding; while graphite forms ionic bond with each other.
exam_questions.option_d: Both graphite and diamond have identical structures and conductivity ran do mly.
exam_questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom is $sp^2$ hybridized in planar sheets, leaving one unhybridized $p$ electron per carbon delocalized across the $\pi$-framework to conduct charge. In diamond, each carbon is $sp^3$ hybridized in a rigid 3D tetrahedral network with all valence electrons locked in localized $\sigma$ bonds.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following lists correctly shows the strength of the intermolecular attractive forces in decreasing order?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{Hydrogen bond} \long right arrow \text{dipole-dipole force} \long right arrow \text{London force}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{Dipole-dipole force} \long right arrow \text{Hydrogen bond} \long right arrow \text{London force}$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{London force} \long right arrow \text{dipole-dipole force} \long right arrow \text{Hydrogen bond}$
exam_questions.option_d: $\text{London force} \long right arrow \text{Hydrogen bond} \long right arrow \text{dipole-dipole force}$
exam_questions.explanation: For molecules of comparable molar mass and size, hydrogen bonds are the strongest intermolecular force ($10-40\text{ kJ/mol}$), followed by dipole-dipole interactions ($5-25\text{ kJ/mol}$), and London dispersion forces ($0.05-40\text{ kJ/mol}$).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: When two chlorine atoms combine to form a chlorine molecule ($\text{Cl}_2$), a covalent bond is formed due to the overlapping of atomic orbitals. Which orbital overlap is responsible for the formation of the bond in $\text{Cl}_2$?
exam_questions.option_a: Side-by-side overlaps of two p orbitals to forms a $\pi$ bond.
exam_questions.option_b: End-to-end overlap of two p orbitals to forms a $\sigma$ bond.
exam_questions.option_c: End-to-end overlaps of two s orbitals to forms a $\sigma$ bond.
exam_questions.option_d: Side-by-side overlap of s orbital and p orbital forms a $\pi$ bond.
exam_questions.explanation: Each chlorine atom has a singly occupied $3p_z$ orbital. The single covalent bond in $\text{Cl}_2$ is formed by the head-on (end-to-end/coaxial) overlap of these two $3p$ orbitals, yielding a cylindrical $\sigma$ (sigma) bond.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: You want to design a set of molecules whose central atoms all exhibit $sp^2$ hybridization. Using concepts of molecular geometry and hybridization, which of the following groups of molecules could best satisfy this requirement?

exam_questions.option_b: $\text{CHCl}_3, \text{C}_6\text{H}_6, \text{C}_2\text{H}_4$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{SO}_2, \text{C}_6\text{H}_6, \text{C}_2\text{H}_4$
exam_questions.explanation: In $\text{SO}_2$, the central sulfur atom has 2 bonded oxygens and 1 lone pair (steric number 3 $\right arrow sp^2$). In benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$), all 6 carbon atoms are $sp^2$ hybridized. In ethene ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$), both carbons are $sp^2$ hybridized.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text:
Given two molecules $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ that satisfy the following conditions:
- Molecule $\text{X}$ contains $14$ sigma ($\sigma$) bonds and no pi ($\pi$) bonds.
- Molecule $\text{Y}$ contains $5$ sigma ($\sigma$) bonds and $0$ pi ($\pi$) bonds. Which of the following molecules can be represented by $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ respectively?
exam_questions.option_a: diethyl ether, $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2)_2\text{O}$ and hydrazine, $(\text{N}_2\text{H}_4)$
exam_questions.option_b: diethyl ether, $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2)_2\text{O}$ and carbon dioxide $(\text{CO}_2)$
exam_questions.option_c: Ethyl alcohol $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH})$ and Benzene $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6)$
exam_questions.explanation: In diethyl ether $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2)_2\text{O}$: there are $2\times (\text{C}-\text{C}) + 2\times (\text{C}-\text{O}) + 10\times (\text{C}-\text{H}) = 14\ \sigma$ bonds and $0\ \pi$ bonds. In hydrazine $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$: there is $1\times (\text{N}-\text{N}) + 4\times (\text{N}-\text{H}) = 5\ \sigma$ bonds and $0\ \pi$ bonds.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on General Principles and Atomic Structure.

exam_questions.question_text: The molecule $\text{BF}_3$ consists of a boron atom bonded to three fluorine atoms. Based on VSEPR theory what is the shape and bond angle of $\text{BF}_3$?
exam_questions.option_a: Tetrahedral $109.5^\circ$ bond angles
exam_questions.option_b: Trigonal planar with $120^\circ$ bond angles
exam_questions.option_c: Linear with $180^\circ$ bond angles
exam_questions.option_d: Bent with bond angles less than $120^\circ$
exam_questions.explanation: Boron has 3 valence electrons and forms 3 single bonds with fluorine with 0 lone pairs. By VSEPR theory, 3 electron domains arrange symmetrically in a trigonal planar geometry with bond angles of $120^\circ$.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle’s law?
exam_questions.option_a: The volume of a gas is directly proportional to temperature at constant pressure.
exam_questions.option_b: The pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume at constant temperature.
exam_questions.option_c: The pressure of a gas is directly proportional to the number of moles at constant temperature.
exam_questions.option_d: The volume of a gas is directly proportional to pressure at constant temperature.
exam_questions.explanation: Boyle's Law states that at constant temperature and fixed amount of gas, the pressure of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its volume ($P \propto 1/V$, or $P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$).

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| \text{B} | sp^2 | sp^2 | sp^2 | sp |

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a pre-condition for a chemical reaction to occur?
exam_questions.option_a: Effective collision
exam_questions.option_b: Sufficient energy.
exam_questions.option_c: proper orientation
exam_questions.explanation: According to Collision Theory, three conditions must be satisfied: reactant particles must collide, with kinetic energy greater than or equal to the activation energy ($E \ge E_a$), and in a proper stereochemical orientation. A 'high activation energy' is an impediment that slows down reactions, not a prerequisite condition.

exam_questions.question_text: Two substances $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ have melting points of $100\ ^\circ\text{C}$ and $50\ ^\circ\text{C}$, respectively. Which substance is more thermally stable as a solid?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{Y}$, because it melts at lower temperature.
exam_questions.option_b: Both are equally stable at the given temperature.
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{X}$, because it requires more heat to melt
exam_questions.explanation: Substance $\text{X}$ has stronger crystal lattice or intermolecular bonding forces, requiring significantly greater thermal energy ($100\ ^\circ\text{C}$) to disrupt its solid structure and transition into liquid state.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following changes will generally increase the rate of a reaction?
exam_questions.option_a: Decreasing temperature of the reaction.
exam_questions.option_b: Decreasing concentration of reactants.
exam_questions.option_c: Using powdered solids instead of large size.
exam_questions.option_d: Removing a catalyst from the reaction.
exam_questions.explanation: Grinding a solid into a fine powder significantly increases the total accessible surface area of the reactant, increasing collision frequency between reactant particles and accelerating the reaction rate.

exam_questions.question_text:
If $K_{c1}$ and $K_{c2}$ are the equilibrium constants for the two reactions:
1. $\text{XeF}_6 (g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{XeOF}_4 (g) + 2\text{HF}(g) \quad K_{c1}$
2. $\text{XeF}_4 (g) + \text{XeF}_6 (g) \rightleftharpoons \text{XeOF}_4 (g) + \text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2 (g) \quad K_{c2}$

What is the equilibrium constant for the reaction:
$$\text{XeF}_4 (g) + 2\text{HF}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{XeO}_3\text{F}_2 (g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$$?
exam_questions.explanation: Reversing reaction (1) gives an equilibrium constant $1/K_{c1}$. Adding the reversed reaction (1) to reaction (2) yields the target reaction. When chemical equations are added, their equilibrium constants are multiplied: $$K = K_{c2} \times \frac{1}{K_{c1}} = \frac{K_{c2}}{K_{c1}}$$

exam_questions.question_text: How is the reaction quotient ($Q_c$) related to equilibrium constant ($K_{eq}$)?
exam_questions.option_a: $Q_c < K_c$ after equilibrium
exam_questions.option_b: $Q_c = K_c$ before equilibrium
exam_questions.option_c: $Q_c = K_c$ at equilibrium
exam_questions.explanation: The reaction quotient $Q_c$ has the same mathematical expression as the equilibrium constant $K_c$ using non-equilibrium concentrations. Exactly when a system reaches dynamic chemical equilibrium, $Q_c = K_c$.

exam_questions.question_text: Which statement best explains why alcohols generally have higher boiling points than alkanes with similar molecular mass?
exam_questions.option_a: Alcohols contain hydroxyl groups that form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
exam_questions.option_b: Alcohols molecules contain carbon atoms that increase intermolecular attractions.
exam_questions.option_c: Alcohols molecules have shorter carbon chains than most similar alkane molecules.
exam_questions.option_d: Alcohols molecules are less polar than alkanes with similar molecular masses.
exam_questions.explanation: Alcohols possess polar hydroxyl ($-OH$) functional groups with highly electronegative oxygen atoms, enabling strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding that requires substantially higher thermal energy to separate.

exam_questions.question_text:
Given the following compounds, what would be the correct decreasing order of boiling point?:
I. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$
II. $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}$
III. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{COOH}$
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{I} > \text{III} > \text{II}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{II} > \text{III} > \text{I}$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{III} > \text{I} > \text{II}$
exam_questions.explanation: All three compounds are structural isomers of hexanoic acid ($C_6H_{12}O_2$). The unbranched straight chain (II) provides the greatest surface area and van der Waals contact, followed by the mono-branched isomer (I), while the highly branched isomer (III) is most compact with the lowest surface area. Thus: $\text{II} > \text{I} > \text{III}$.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following describes a general method for synthesizing esters from carboxylic acids and alcohols, emphasizing reaction conditions and equilibrium?
exam_questions.option_a: Mixing alcohol and carboxylic acid without catalyst.
exam_questions.option_b: Carboxylic acids and alcohols are reacted under basic condition
exam_questions.option_c: Heating of carboxylic acid and alcohol with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
exam_questions.option_d: Esters formed only by oxidation of alcohols in the presence of $\text{Cu}$.
exam_questions.explanation: Fischer esterification involves heating a carboxylic acid and alcohol under reflux in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, which acts as an acid catalyst and a dehydrating agent to drive the equilibrium toward ester formation.

exam_questions.question_text: Which evaluation correctly describe physical and chemical properties of oils?
exam_questions.option_a: Oils are solids and remain unreactive under all conditions.
exam_questions.option_b: Oils are polar solid and can’t decompose when exposed to air.
exam_questions.option_c: Oils are generally liquid undergo hydrogenation reaction
exam_questions.option_d: Oils are nonpolar liquids but cannot react with acids and bases
exam_questions.explanation: Plant and vegetable oils are triglycerides rich in unsaturated fatty acids with double bonds (rendering them liquid at room temperature). They undergo catalytic hydrogenation (addition of $H_2$) to form saturated solid fats like margarine.

exam_questions.question_text: Why tricarboxylic acids have higher boiling points than monocarboxylic acids?
exam_questions.option_a: Monocarboxylic acids are branched, lowering the boiling point.
exam_questions.option_b: Tricarboxylic acids are lighter, which increases boiling points.
exam_questions.option_c: Monocarboxylic acids contain double bonds, reducing its boiling point
exam_questions.option_d: The more –$\text{COOH}$ in tricarboxylic acid, forming stronger hydrogen bonds
exam_questions.explanation: Tricarboxylic acids contain three carboxyl groups ($-COOH$), facilitating an extensive 3D network of multiple intermolecular hydrogen bonds as well as higher molecular mass.

exam_questions.question_text: In a redox reaction: $\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{HCl} \long right arrow \text{MnCl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the roles of the reactants?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{MnO}_2$ is the reducing agent because the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ increases.
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{HCl}$ is the oxidizing agent because the oxidation state of $\text{Cl}$ increases.
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{MnO}_2$ is the oxidizing agent because the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ decreases
exam_questions.option_d: $\text{HCl}$ is the reducing agent because the oxidation state of $\text{H}$ decreases.
exam_questions.explanation: The oxidation state of manganese drops from $+4$ in $\text{MnO}_2$ to $+2$ in $\text{MnCl}_2$ (reduction). Hence, $\text{MnO}_2$ is the oxidizing agent.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on Physical Chemistry, Kinetics, and Equilibrium.

exam_questions.question_text: When $5.0\text{ g}$ of magnesium reacts with $20.0\text{ g}$ of oxygen gas according to the reaction: $$2\text{Mg}(s) + \text{O}_2 (g) \right arrow 2\text{MgO}(s)$$ What is the mass of $\text{MgO}$ that can be formed?
exam_questions.explanation: Molar mass of $\text{Mg} = 24.3\text{ g/mol}$, $\text{O}_2 = 32.0\text{ g/mol}$, and $\text{MgO} = 40.3\text{ g/mol}$. Moles of $\text{Mg} = 5.0 / 24.3 = 0.2058\text{ mol}$; moles of $\text{O}_2 = 20.0 / 32.0 = 0.625\text{ mol}$. Magnesium is the limiting reactant. Yield: $$0.2058\text{ mol} \times 40.3\text{ g/mol} = 8.29\text{ g} \approx 8.3\text{ g}$$

exam_questions.question_text: A student crushes a large crystal of sugar into many small pieces before dissolving it in water. The sugar dissolves faster than the large crystal. Which of the following is correctly describing the observation?
exam_questions.option_a: Increase in intermolecular force
exam_questions.option_b: Increase the surface area of the molecule
exam_questions.option_c: Increase in pressure of the system
exam_questions.explanation: Subdividing a large crystal into smaller particles increases the surface area exposed to the surrounding solvent molecules, accelerating the dissolution process.

exam_questions.question_text: A technician prepares a solution by dissolving $40\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$, in enough water to make $500\text{ mL}$ of solution. What is the molarity ($\text{M}$) of this solution?
exam_questions.explanation: Molar mass of $\text{NaOH} = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40.0\text{ g/mol}$. Moles of $\text{NaOH} = 40\text{ g} / 40\text{ g/mol} = 1.0\text{ mol}$. Volume = $500\text{ mL} = 0.500\text{ L}$. Molarity $$M = \frac{1.0\text{ mol}}{0.500\text{ L}} = 2.0\text{ M}$$

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following oxides is classified as an amphoteric oxide?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{CaO}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{SO}_2$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$
exam_questions.explanation: Aluminum oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) is an amphoteric oxide because it can react with both strong acids (forming aluminum salts) and strong bases (forming aluminate ions).

exam_questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements correctly applies to the formation and nature of salts?
I. $\text{NaHSO}_4$ is a normal salt because all ionizable $\text{H}^+$ from the acid are replaced. II. $\text{NaHSO}_4$ is acidic salt formed when ionizable $\text{H}^+$ of the acid is not completely replaced by metal ions. III. $\text{Zn (OH) Cl}$ is a basic salt because it contains one ionizable $\text{OH}^-$ group in its formula. IV. $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a basic salt due to the presence of $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ that can be hydrolysis.
exam_questions.option_a: Only IV
exam_questions.option_b: Only II
exam_questions.option_c: II, III & IV
exam_questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect because $\text{NaHSO}_4$ has an unreplaced ionizable proton. Statements II (acid salt), III (basic salt with hydroxy group), and IV (salt of strong base + weak acid that undergoes anion hydrolysis to yield alkaline solution) are all correct.

exam_questions.question_text: In a Galvanic cell consisting of Zinc and Copper elect rodes, which of the following process occurs at the anode electrode?
exam_questions.option_a: Reduction half-cell reaction is takes placed
exam_questions.option_b: Copper ions are reduced to Copper metal.
exam_questions.option_c: Electrons flow from Copper to Zinc.
exam_questions.option_d: Zinc metal is oxidized to Zinc ions.
exam_questions.explanation: In a Daniell galvanic cell, the anode is the negative electrode where oxidation takes place: $\text{Zn}(s) \right arrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + 2e^-$.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correctly describing the reaction represented in the diagram below?
exam_questions.option_a: It is an endothermic reaction with a positive $\Delta\text{H}$.
exam_questions.option_b: Energy is absorbed from the surroundings.
exam_questions.option_c: It is an exothermic reaction with a negative $\Delta\text{H}$.
exam_questions.option_d: Heat is neither released nor absorbed in this reaction
exam_questions.explanation: In the potential energy diagram, the enthalpy of the products is lower than that of the reactants ($H_{\text{products}} < H_{\text{reactants}}$), so $\Delta H = H_p - H_r < 0$, signifying an exothermic reaction that releases heat.

exam_questions.question_text: In the extraction of Iron using a blast furnace, what is the primary purpose of adding Limestone ($\text{CaCO}_3$) to the furnace?
exam_questions.option_a: Act as a reducing agent for the iron ore.
exam_questions.option_b: Provide the heat necessary for the reaction.
exam_questions.option_c: Remove impurities like silica ($\text{SiO}_2$)
exam_questions.explanation: Limestone thermally decomposes into calcium oxide ($\text{CaO}$), which acts as a basic flux reacting with acidic sand/silica impurities ($\text{SiO}_2$) to form molten calcium silicate slag ($\text{CaSiO}_3$) that floats and is tapped off.

exam_questions.question_text: Non-metals usually have poor electrical conductivity and are often brittle. However, they are widely used in electrical insulation and chemical industries. Which evaluation best explain how these properties affect their real-world uses?
exam_questions.option_a: Non-metals are unsuitable for all industrial applications because they are brittle.
exam_questions.option_b: Non-metals are useful as electrical insulators but their brittleness limited their use
exam_questions.option_c: Non-metals are mainly used for construction because they are strong and malleable
exam_questions.option_d: Non-metals are good electrical and heat conductors like metal
exam_questions.explanation: Because non-metals lack free mobile valence electrons, they are non-conductive and serve as vital electrical insulators, though their mechanical brittleness limits their utility in load-bearing structural tasks.

exam_questions.question_text: What is the correct IUPAC name for this molecule?
exam_questions.option_a: 4,4-diethyl-3,4-dibromo-5-methyl decane
exam_questions.option_b: 7,8-dibromo-6,6-diethyl-8-methyl decane
exam_questions.option_c: 4,4-diethyl-3,4-dibromo-3-methyl decane
exam_questions.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain contains 10 carbons (decane). Numbering from the left gives substituents at positions 3, 4, and 5. Alphabetical ordering: bromo before diethyl before methyl yields 3,4-dibromo-5,5-diethyl-3-methyldecane.

exam_questions.question_text: Abel is a grade 10 student. He took three different test tubes and added $5.00\text{ mL}$ of toluene to each test tube. Then he added 2 drops of $\text{Br}_2$ water in the first test tube, equal drops of cold $\text{KMnO}_4$ in the second test tube and again equal drops of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the third test tube. In which test tube does a reaction occur?
exam_questions.option_a: The 1st and the 3rd test tube
exam_questions.option_b: The 2nd test tube and the 3rd test tube
exam_questions.option_c: The 3rd test tube
exam_questions.explanation: Toluene is an aromatic hydrocarbon that does not react with aqueous bromine water without a Lewis acid catalyst/UV light, nor does it react with cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_4$ (oxidation of the methyl side chain requires heating). However, toluene undergoes electrophilic aromatic sulfonation with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at room temperature.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is the major limit ation of the Arrhenius concept of acids and bases?
exam_questions.option_a: It is limited to aqueous solutions
exam_questions.option_b: It explains proton transfer
exam_questions.option_c: It includes Lewis acid-base reactions
exam_questions.explanation: The Arrhenius theory restricts acids and bases strictly to substances that dissociate to produce $\text{H}^+$ or $\text{OH}^-$ ions in water (aqueous medium), failing to account for acid-base behaviors in gas phases or non-aqueous solvents.

exam_questions.question_text: A grade 12 student prepares $0.20\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of Acetic acid in the laboratory, according to the ionization equation given: $$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+(aq) + \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-(aq): K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$$ Which of the following is the closest approximation of the hydrogen ion concentration? (Given $\sqrt{3.6} = 1.9$)
exam_questions.explanation: For a weak monoprotic acid: $$[\text{H}^+] = \sqrt{K_a \cdot C_a} = \sqrt{1.8 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.20} = \sqrt{3.6 \times 10^{-6}} = 1.9 \times 10^{-3}\text{ M}$$

exam_questions.question_text: Consider a solution that is $0.10\text{ M}$ acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and $0.20\text{ M}$ sodium acetate ($\text{NaCH}_3\text{COO}$). Which of the following statements is correct?
exam_questions.option_a: Adding a small amount of $\text{NaOH}$ causes the $\text{pH}$ to decrease slightly.
exam_questions.option_b: When $\text{NaOH}$ is added, the $\text{OH}^-$ ions react with $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$ ions.
exam_questions.option_c: Adding a small amount of $\text{HCl}$ causes the $\text{pH}$ to decrease slightly.
exam_questions.option_d: When $\text{HCl}$ is added, the $\text{H}^+$ ions react with $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ molecules.
exam_questions.explanation: This is an acidic buffer solution. Adding a small amount of strong acid ($\text{HCl}$) is buffered by acetate ions ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+ \right arrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$), resulting in only a slight decrease in $\text{pH}$.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following procedure can NOT produce buffer solution?
exam_questions.option_a: Equal volume of $0.5\text{M } \text{NaOH}$ and $1\text{M } \text{HCl}$ solution are mixed.
exam_questions.option_b: Equal volume of $0.5\text{M } \text{NaOH}$ and $1\text{M } \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ solution are mixed.
exam_questions.option_c: Equal volume of $1\text{M } \text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ and $1\text{M } \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ solution are mixed.
exam_questions.option_d: Equal volume of $1\text{M } \text{NH}_3$ and $0.5\text{M } \text{HCl}$ solution are mixed.
exam_questions.explanation: Mixing $\text{NaOH}$ with excess strong acid $\text{HCl}$ produces $\text{NaCl}$ and residual $\text{HCl}$. Since both are strong electrolytes with no weak conjugate pair, it cannot function as a buffer.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on Electrochemistry, Industrial Chemistry, and Organic Chemistry.

exam_questions.question_text: A buffer solution is prepared using Acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) and its conjugate base Sodium acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$). Under which condition will this buffer solution have maximum buffering capacity?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{pH} = \text{pK}_a$
exam_questions.explanation: Maximum buffer capacity occurs when the concentrations of weak acid and conjugate base are equal ($[\text{HA}] = [\text{A}^-]$), at which point $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a$ according to the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following salts will produce an acidic solution when dissolved in water?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{NaCl}$
exam_questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) is the salt of a weak base ($\text{NH}_3$) and a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$). The $\text{NH}_4^+$ cat i on hydrolyzes in water to produce hydronium ions: $\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$.

exam_questions.question_text: The dye bromothymol blue ($\text{HBb}$) is a weak acid whose ionization can be represented as follows: $$\text{HBb}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+(aq) + \text{Bb}^-(aq)$$ Which way will the equilibrium shift when $\text{NaOH}$ is added?
exam_questions.option_a: Initially to the left, finally to right
exam_questions.option_b: Initially to the right finally to left
exam_questions.option_c: To the left
exam_questions.explanation: Adding $\text{NaOH}$ introduces hydroxide ions ($\text{OH}^-$), which react with $\text{H}^+$ to form water. By Le Chatelier's Principle, removing $\text{H}^+$ shifts the equilibrium to the right.

exam_questions.question_text: During laboratory class, a student placed clean water in a beaker and added pieces of calcium metal using tongs. Which of the following is observed color after the reaction has completed?
exam_questions.option_a: The litmus paper turns to blue.
exam_questions.option_b: The litmus paper turns to red.
exam_questions.option_c: The litmus paper maintains its color.
exam_questions.option_d: The litmus paper turns to colorless
exam_questions.explanation: Calcium reacts with water to form basic calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas: $\text{Ca}(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \right arrow \text{Ca (OH)}_2 (aq) + \text{H}_2 (g)$. The resulting alkaline solution turns red litmus paper blue.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is NOT correctly describe about oxidation and reduction?
exam_questions.option_a: oxidizing agent is a species being reduced and causes oxidation
exam_questions.option_b: Reducing agent is a species being oxidized and causes reduction.
exam_questions.option_c: Oxidation is gain of electron while reduction is loss of electrons
exam_questions.option_d: Oxidation and reduction reactions are occurs simultaneously
exam_questions.explanation: By definition (OIL RIG): Oxidation is the Loss of electrons, and Reduction is the Gain of electrons. Statement C incorrectly reverses this definition.

exam_questions.question_text: A chemist compares electrolysis of dilute $\text{NaCl}$ solution and concentrated $\text{NaCl}$ solution using inert elect rodes. The substance produced at anode electrode of dilute $\text{NaCl}$ solution and concentrated $\text{NaCl}$ solution are _____ and _____ respectively.
exam_questions.option_a: Oxygen and chlorine.
exam_questions.option_b: chlorine and chlorine
exam_questions.option_c: hydrogen and chlorine
exam_questions.explanation: In dilute $\text{NaCl}$ solution, water oxidation dominates at the anode producing Oxygen ($\text{O}_2$). In concentrated $\text{NaCl}$ (brine), chloride ion discharge is favored due to high concentration and chlorine over potential, producing Chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on Electrochemistry, Industrial Chemistry, and Organic Chemistry.

exam_questions.question_text: An aqueous solution contains $\text{Ag}^+(aq)$ and $\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)$ ions. Electrolysis is carried out using inert platinum elect rodes. A constant current of $9.65\text{ A}$ is passed through the solution for $1000\text{ seconds}$. Which metal will be deposited at the cathode and what mass will be deposited?
exam_questions.option_a: Copper, $10.8\text{ g}$
exam_questions.option_b: Silver, $10.8\text{ g}$
exam_questions.option_c: Silver, $5.4\text{ g}$
exam_questions.explanation: Because $E^\circ(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}) = +0.80\text{ V} > E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}$, silver ions reduce first at the cathode. Charge $Q = I \times t = 9.65\text{ A} \times 1000\text{ s} = 9650\text{ C} = 0.10\text{ mol } e^-$. Moles of $\text{Ag} = 0.10\text{ mol}$. Mass $= 0.10\text{ mol} \times 108\text{ g/mol} = 10.8\text{ g}$.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Answer questions based on Electrochemistry, Industrial Chemistry, and Organic Chemistry.

exam_questions.question_text: A Galvanic cell constructed from a strip of magnesium metal dipped in a solution of magnesium sulfate and a strip of silver metal immersed in a solution of silver nitrate. Which of the following correctly represents the cell not ation for this galvanic cell?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{Ag} /\text{Ag}^+ //\text{Mg}^{2+} / \text{Mg}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{Mg} /\text{Mg}^{2+} // \text{Ag}^+ /\text{Ag}$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{Mg} /\text{Mg}^{2+}/ \text{Ag}^+ / \text{Ag}$
exam_questions.explanation: By convention, the anode (oxidation of $\text{Mg}$) is written on the left, followed by the double vertical line for the salt bridge, and the cathode (reduction of $\text{Ag}^+$) on the right: $\text{Mg} | \text{Mg}^{2+} || \text{Ag}^+ | \text{Ag}$.

exam_questions.question_text: Statement: Currently, many workers in the company have become punctual. Assumption I: All the workers must have bought their own automobiles. Assumption II: Previously, many of the workers were late to work. Assumption III: Employers are now more serious about lateness to work. Assumption IV: The productivity of the company has become questionable. Which one of the assumptions is logically related with the above statement?
exam_questions.option_a: Assumptions II and III
exam_questions.option_b: Assumptions I and II
exam_questions.option_c: Assumptions III and IV
exam_questions.explanation: When workers suddenly " become punctual," it inherently presumes they were frequently tardy before (Assumption II). In organizational behavior, such widespread behavioral corrections typically stem from management taking strict administrative measures against tardiness (Assumption III). Therefore, Assumptions II and III are directly and logically related.

exam_questions.question_text: Ms. Y is Ms. X ' s mother, and Mr. P is Ms. Y ' s only brother. Mr. Z is Mr. P ' s son. Thus, how is Mr. Z related to Ms. X?
exam_questions.option_a: niece
exam_questions.option_b: uncle
exam_questions.option_c: nephew
exam_questions.explanation: Ms. Y is Ms. X ' s mother. Mr. P is Ms. Y ' s brother, which makes Mr. P the maternal uncle of Ms. X. Mr. Z is the son of Mr. P (the uncle's child). Therefore, Mr. Z and Ms. X are first cousins (maternal cousins).

exam_questions.question_text: Statement: Many universities are replacing printed resources with on line resources. Therefore, students can have better access for resources to learn effectively. Based on the above statement, which one of the following options is valid?

exam_questions.option_b: Universities are giving priority to save money.
exam_questions.option_c: Printed resources are better than digital resources.
exam_questions.option_d: On line resources enhance students' learning.
options: Universities are giving priority to save money.
Printed resources are better than digital resources.
exam_questions.explanation: The prompt explicitly states that replacing printed materials with on line resources allows students to " have better access for resources to learn effectively," directly establishing that on line resources enhance students' learning.

exam_questions.question_text: Statement: Sheep, animals and furry animals exist. All sheep are furry animals. All animals are not sheep. Conclusion I: Some animals are furry animals. Conclusion II: All furry animals are sheep. Conclusion III: No animals are furry animals. Conclusion IV: No furry animals are animals. Which of the above conclusions can be logically drawn from the preceding statement?
exam_questions.option_a: Conclusions I and II
exam_questions.option_b: Conclusion IV
exam_questions.option_c: Conclusion I
exam_questions.explanation: All sheep are animals and all sheep are furry animals. Because the set of sheep is non-empty and constitutes a subset of animals that are furry, it logically follows that " Some animals are furry animals " (Conclusion I).

exam_questions.reading_passage: Passage I: The growing influence of social media has created significant responsibilities for both platform designers and users. Central to this responsibility are digital literacy, critical thinking, and ethical engagement. Users must be equipped with the skills to evaluate information sources, recognize persuasive techniques, and engage thoughtfully with on line content. Looking ahead, advancements such as artificial intelligence, immersive media, and augmented reality are expected to further transform how social media influence operates by enabling more personalized and interactive experiences. exam_questions.reading_passage: Passage II: People often believe that successful individuals share three main qualities: motivation, ability, and opportunity. According to this view, success comes from hard work, natural talent, and a bit of luck. However, these factors alone do not fully explain why some people succeed more than others. An important factor that is often over looked is how people interact with others. In everyday work situations, individuals must decide whether to focus only on their own benefit or to help others without expecting immediate rewards. Studies of different organizations reveal that people have different attitudes toward giving and receiving help. Some people prefer to take more than they give, while others prefer to support and cooperate with those around them. These differences affect how people build relationships and achieve their goals in the work place. Those who focus mainly on their own interests often see the world as very competitive. They believe that to succeed, they must always be better than others. As a result, they try to make their achievements visible and protect their own interests. Although they are not necessarily unkind, they tend to act carefully and put themselves first. Others, however, are more willing to consider the needs of their colleagues, even if it means delaying their own success. These different ways of interacting show that success depends not only on personal effort but also on how people treat others. (Source: Adapted from Grant, A. (2013) Give and Take: A Revolutionary Approach to Success. New York: Viking, p. 3)

exam_questions.question_text: Consider the parallelogram ABCD. If DC = 10 cm, M and N are midpoints of DC and AB respectively, and the area of triangle ADM is 20 cm², then what is the area of parallelogram ANCM in cm²?

Solving for height h: 2.5 * h = 20 ⇒ h = 8 cm. Parallelogram ANCM has base MC = 5 cm and the same perpendicular height h = 8 cm. Area (ANCM) = base * height = 5 * 8 = 40 cm².

exam_questions.question_text:
Let x - y = 2, and x² + y² = 10, where x, y ∈ ℝ and x > 0, y > 0. Quantity A: x⁴ + y⁴ - 9/(xy) Quantity B: 79
Which one of the following is true?
exam_questions.option_a: Quantity B is greater than Quantity A.
exam_questions.option_b: The relationship cannot be determined.
exam_questions.option_c: Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
exam_questions.option_d: Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.
options: Quantity B is greater than Quantity A.
Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.
exam_questions.explanation:
1) Squaring (x - y): (x - y)² = x² - 2xy + y² ⇒ 2² = (x² + y²) - 2xy ⇒ 4 = 10 - 2xy ⇒ 2xy = 6 ⇒ xy = 3.
2) Squaring (x² + y²): (x² + y²)² = x⁴ + 2 (xy)² + y⁴ ⇒ 10² = (x⁴ + y⁴) + 2 (3²) ⇒ 100 = (x⁴ + y⁴) + 18 ⇒ x⁴ + y⁴ = 82.
3) Evaluating Quantity A: (x⁴ + y⁴) - 9/(xy) = 82 - 9/3 = 82 - 3 = 79. Since Quantity A = 79 and Quantity B = 79, Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.

exam_questions.question_text:
Let △DCE be a right-angled triangle with right angle at D that inscribes a circle with center O and radius r = 5 m. The side DC is 12 m long and all sides are tangent to the circle. Quantity A: The length of side CE (hypotenuse) Quantity B: 36 meters
Which one of the following is true?
exam_questions.option_a: Quantity B is greater than Quantity A.
exam_questions.option_b: Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.
exam_questions.option_c: Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
options: Quantity B is greater than Quantity A.
Quantity A is equal to Quantity B.
Quantity A is greater than Quantity B.
exam_questions.explanation:
For a right triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c, the inradius formula is r = (a + b - c)/2. Here, leg a = DC = 12 m, r = 5 m, leg b = DE, and hypotenuse c = √(12² + b²).
5 = (12 + b - √(144 + b²))/2 ⇒ 10 = 12 + b - √(144 + b²) ⇒ √(144 + b²) = b + 2. Squaring both sides: 144 + b² = b² + 4b + 4 ⇒ 140 = 4b ⇒ b = 35 m. Hypotenuse CE = c = √(12² + 35²) = √(144 + 1225) = √1369 = 37 m. Since Quantity A (CE = 37 m) is greater than Quantity B (36 m), Quantity A is greater.

exam_questions.question_text: A person has a fencing material of length 100m. He wants to enclose a rectangular region for his dogs and also needs to have a 2m gate at one corner. What is the maximum area he can enclose in m²?
exam_questions.option_c: 625 m²
exam_questions.explanation:
The total perimeter of the rectangular fence minus the 2 m un-fenced gate is 100 m:
2x + 2y - 2 = 100 ⇒ 2 (x + y) = 102 ⇒ x + y = 51. To maximize area A = x * y with x + y = 51, we choose a square where x = y = 51/2 = 25.5 m. Maximum Area = (51/2)² = 2601 / 4 m² = 650.25 m².

exam_questions.question_text: If x : y : z = 2 : 3 : 5 and y = 60, then what is the value of x + z?
exam_questions.explanation: Let the common scaling factor be k: y = 3k = 60 ⇒ k = 20. Then x = 2k = 2 * 20 = 40, and z = 5k = 5 * 20 = 100. Sum x + z = 40 + 100 = 140.

exam_questions.question_text: If the roots of the quadratic equation x² - mx + k = 0 are two consecutive integers, then what is the value of m² - 4k?
exam_questions.explanation:
Let the consecutive roots be n and n + 1. By Vieta's formulas: Sum of roots m = n + (n + 1) = 2n + 1. Product of roots k = n (n + 1) = n² + n. Now calculate m² - 4k:
(2n + 1)² - 4 (n² + n) = (4n² + 4n + 1) - (4n² + 4n) = 1.

exam_questions.question_text: If two six faces dice are thrown together, then what is the probability that the two numbers on the upper faces are NOT relatively prime?
exam_questions.explanation:
Total outcomes = 6 * 6 = 36. Pairs with gcd (a, b) > 1 (not coprime):
- Even pairs (gcd ≥ 2): (2,2), (2,4), (2,6), (4,2), (4,4), (4,6), (6,2), (6,4), (6,6) → 9 pairs
- Divisible by 3 (not both even): (3,3), (3,6), (6,3) → 3 pairs
- Divisible by 5: (5,5) → 1 pair
Total pairs that are NOT relatively prime = 9 + 3 + 1 = 13 pairs. Probability = 13/36.

exam_questions.question_text:

Row 1 (base): [4, 2, 3, 7]
Row 2: [5, 4, 9]
Row 3: [8, 12]
Row 4 (top): [x] 
Which one of the following numbers is the value of x?

exam_questions.question_text: By using a certain formula using a digit number 12345 we obtained 29 and using some pattern from the digit number 23456 we obtained 126 then which one of the following numbers is obtained from the digit number 3456?
exam_questions.explanation: The arithmetic pattern is: multiply all digits except the last one, then add the last digit. For 12345: (1 * 2 * 3 * 4) + 5 = 24 + 5 = 29. For 23456: (2 * 3 * 4 * 5) + 6 = 120 + 6 = 126. For 3456: (3 * 4 * 5) + 6 = 60 + 6 = 66.

exam_questions.question_text: Consider a circle that has diameter AB of length 8 cm. If you fold the circle over AB, then what is the area of the part of the circle on one part of the diameter (in cm²)?
exam_questions.option_a: 8π
exam_questions.explanation: Given diameter d = 8 cm, the radius r = 4 cm. Total area of the circle = πr² = π(4)² = 16π cm². Folding the circle across its diameter AB divides the circle into two identical semicircles. The area of one semicircular part = (16π) / 2 = 8π cm².

exam_questions.question_text: In how many different ways can 6 people be seated at a round table?
exam_questions.explanation: The number of circular permutations of n distinct objects is given by (n - 1)!. For n = 6: (6 - 1)! = 5! = 5 * 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 120 ways.

exam_questions.question_text:

exam_questions.question_text: When the circle (x - 3)² + (y - 1)² = 1 is reflected on a line y = 2x, then the image of the circle is:

The radius remains r = 1 under reflect i on (i some try). Therefore, the image circle equation is (x - (-1))² + (y - 3)² = 1 ⇒ (x + 1)² + (y - 3)² = 1.

exam_questions.question_text: Let f (x) = x³ + 3x² - 9x + 7. Then, the graph of f is decreasing on:
exam_questions.explanation:
A function is decreasing where its first derivative f'(x) ≤ 0.
f'(x) = 3x² + 6x - 9 = 3 (x² + 2x - 3) = 3 (x + 3)(x - 1). Setting 3 (x + 3)(x - 1) ≤ 0 yields the closed interval [-3, 1].

exam_questions.question_text: A person deposits Birr 6000 at the end of each year into a saving account that pays 10% interest compounded annually. What is the future value of the annuity after 3 years?

exam_questions.explanation:

exam_questions.question_text: What are the vertex and line of symmetry of the function y = 2x² - 4x + 3 respectively?
exam_questions.explanation:
For a quadratic y = ax² + bx + c:
x-coordinate of vertex = -b / (2a) = -(-4) / (2 * 2) = 4 / 4 = 1.
y-coordinate = 2 (1)² - 4 (1) + 3 = 2 - 4 + 3 = 1. Vertex is (1, 1) and the vertical axis of symmetry is x = 1.

exam_questions.question_text: Consider the circle centered at O, and a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD in the circle where angle A = (x + 40)°, angle B = 2x°, angle C = (2x - 10)°, and angle D = y°. What is the value of y?
exam_questions.explanation:
In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite interior angles are supplementary (sum to 180°):
1) ∠A + ∠C = 180° ⇒ (x + 40) + (2x - 10) = 180° ⇒ 3x + 30 = 180° ⇒ 3x = 150° ⇒ x = 50°.
2) ∠B + ∠D = 180° ⇒ 2x + y = 180° ⇒ 2 (50°) + y = 180° ⇒ 100° + y = 180° ⇒ y = 80°.

exam_questions.question_text: An outcome of a random experiment is said to be a favorable outcome if:

exam_questions.question_text: Let L and S be the largest and smallest values of the given data respectively. The coefficient of range of the data is a relative measure given by:

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about a given natural number?

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the use of standard deviation?

exam_questions.question_text: What is the simplified form of the expression ((x + 3)/x ÷ (x - 2)/(x - 3)) * ((x² - 2x)/(x² - 9)) over its domain?
exam_questions.explanation:
Step 1: Invert and multiply the division part:
((x + 3)/x) * ((x - 3)/(x - 2)) = [(x + 3)(x - 3)] / [x (x - 2)] = (x² - 9) / [x (x - 2)]. Step 2: Multiply by the second term:
[(x² - 9) / (x (x - 2))] * [x (x - 2) / (x² - 9)] = 1.

exam_questions.question_text: Water is being poured into a circular cylinder of radius 50 cm at a rate of change of volume 5000π cm³/sec. What is the rate of change of height of the level of water in the cylinder when the height is 40 cm?

exam_questions.option_b: 1/100 cm/sec
exam_questions.option_c: 10 cm/sec

Volume of a cylinder: V = πr²h. Since radius r = 50 cm is constant:
V = π(50)²h = 2500π h. Different i ating with respect to time t:
dV/dt = 2500π (dh/dt).
5000π = 2500π (dh/dt) ⇒ dh/dt = 5000π / 2500π = 2 cm/sec.

exam_questions.question_text: A contest offers 17 prizes. The first prize is worth Birr 6,000 and each successive prize is worth Birr 300 less than the preceding prize. What is the total value of the prizes in Birr?
exam_questions.explanation:
This forms an Arithmetic Progress i on with first term a = 6000, common difference d = -300, and number of terms n = 17. Sum Sₙ = (n/2) * [2a + (n - 1) d]
S₁₇ = (17/2) * [2 (6000) + 16(-300)] = (17/2) * [12000 - 4800] = (17/2) * 7200 = 17 * 3600 = 61,200 Birr.

exam_questions.question_text: A company manufactures two products P and Q. Product P requires 2 hours on machine A and 1 hour on machine B. Product Q requires 1 hour on machine A and 1 hour on machine B. Machine A is available for at most 10 hours a day. Machine B is available for at most 8 hours a day. The profit for product P is Birr 40. The profit for product Q is Birr 30. How many units of P and Q should be produced to maximize the profit?
exam_questions.option_a: 4 units of P and 5 units of Q
exam_questions.option_b: 10 units of P and 2 units of Q
exam_questions.option_c: 2 units of P and 6 units of Q
exam_questions.option_d: 4 units of P and 8 units of Q
options: 4 units of P and 5 units of Q
10 units of P and 2 units of Q
2 units of P and 6 units of Q
4 units of P and 8 units of Q
exam_questions.explanation:
Objective: Maximize Z = 40P + 30Q. Constraints: 2P + Q ≤ 10, P + Q ≤ 8, P ≥ 0, Q ≥ 0. Corner points:
1. (0, 0) ⇒ Z = 0
2. (5, 0) ⇒ Z = 40 (5) = 200
3. (0, 8) ⇒ Z = 30 (8) = 240
4. Intersection of 2P + Q = 10 and P + Q = 8:
Subtracting equations: P = 2, so Q = 8 - 2 = 6. Z (2, 6) = 40 (2) + 30 (6) = 80 + 180 = 260 Birr (Maximum profit). Therefore, producing 2 units of P and 6 units of Q maximizes profit.

exam_questions.question_text:

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the degree of the polynomial function f defined by f (x) = x²(x - 4)(x² + 2)?

Degree = 2 + 1 + 2 = 5.

exam_questions.question_text: Given a regular square pyramid with base edge 8 cm and slant height 5 cm. What is the total surface area in cm²?
exam_questions.explanation: Base area = s² = 8² = 64 cm². Lateral surface area = 4 * (1/2 * base * slant height) = 4 * (1/2 * 8 * 5) = 80 cm². Total Surface Area = Base Area + Lateral Area = 64 + 80 = 144 cm².

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about homogeneity of system of linear equations?

The system x + y = 0, x + 2y + 3z = 0, z = 0 is nonhomogeneous.
exam_questions.explanation: A system of linear equations Ax = b is defined as homogeneous if and only if all constant terms on the right-hand side are zero (b = 0). System B satisfies this definition identically.

exam_questions.question_text: If f (x) = ln (x² + 1) and g (x) = eˣ, then (f ∘ g)'(0) is equal to:

(f ∘ g)'(x) = 2e²ˣ / (e²ˣ + 1). Evaluating at x = 0:
(f ∘ g)'(0) = 2e⁰ / (e⁰ + 1) = 2 (1) / (1 + 1) = 2 / 2 = 1.

The set of all values of k for which the system of equations:
x + y + z = 1

is consistent is:

exam_questions.question_text: If u is a vector with initial point (2, 1) and terminal point (-4, 3), then which one of the following is equal to the vector u?

exam_questions.question_text: Let f (x) = x / (x² + 3x + 1). Then, f'(x) is equal to:
exam_questions.explanation:
Using the Quotient Rule: d/dx [u/v] = (u'v - uv') / v²
Here u = x ⇒ u' = 1, v = x² + 3x + 1 ⇒ v' = 2x + 3.
f'(x) = [1 * (x² + 3x + 1) - x * (2x + 3)] / (x² + 3x + 1)²
= (x² + 3x + 1 - 2x² - 3x) / (x² + 3x + 1)² = (1 - x²) / (x² + 3x + 1)².

exam_questions.question_text: A shopkeeper wants to increase his profit from Birr 3000 to Birr 3600. By what percent will his profit increase?

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following sets represents an empty set?

exam_questions.question_text: Let f (x) = 6x⁶ + 4x⁴ + 3x² + 2 and g (x) = 3x² + 2. Then which one of the following is equal to f (x) / g (x)?

exam_questions.question_text: What is the value of the integral from 0 to π of sin³(x) cos (x) dx?

exam_questions.question_text: What is the sum of the series Σ(n=1 to ∞) 1 / (n (n + 1))?
exam_questions.explanation:
Using partial fraction decomposition:
1 / [n (n + 1)] = 1/n - 1/(n + 1). The partial sum S_N = (1 - 1/2) + (1/2 - 1/3) + ... + (1/N - 1/(N + 1)) = 1 - 1/(N + 1). Taking the limit as N → ∞:
Sum = lim_{N→∞} [1 - 1/(N + 1)] = 1 - 0 = 1.

exam_questions.question_text: The school management wants to study grade eleven students' performance. There are ten sections of grade eleven in the school. Three sections of grade eleven are ran do mly selected and ALL students in these three sections are taken as the sample. Which one of the following is the sampling technique used?
exam_questions.option_a: Multistage sampling technique
exam_questions.option_b: Cluster sampling method
exam_questions.option_c: Stratified sampling technique
exam_questions.explanation: In cluster sampling, the entire population is divided into natural groups (clusters/sections), a random sample of whole clusters is selected, and every single member within the chosen clusters is surveyed.

exam_questions.question_text:
What are the minimum and the maximum values of z = 2x + 3y subject to the constraints:
x + y ≥ 2
x + y ≤ 5
2y - x ≤ 4
x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0
respectively?
exam_questions.option_a: 4 and 13
exam_questions.option_b: 6 and 10
exam_questions.option_c: 4 and 10
exam_questions.explanation:
Feasible region vertices:
1. (2, 0) ⇒ z = 2 (2) + 3 (0) = 4 (Minimum value) 2. (5, 0) ⇒ z = 2 (5) + 3 (0) = 10
3. Intersection of x + y = 5 and 2y - x = 4: Adding gives 3y = 9 ⇒ y = 3, x = 2 ⇒ (2, 3) ⇒ z = 2 (2) + 3 (3) = 4 + 9 = 13 (Maximum value) 4. (0, 2) ⇒ z = 2 (0) + 3 (2) = 6. Minimum = 4 and Maximum = 13.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a convergent series?
exam_questions.explanation: For a geometric series Σ a*r^(k-1) to converge, the absolute value of the common ratio |r| must be strictly less than 1. In D: 2^(k + 1) / 5^(k - 1) = 2² * (2/5)^(k - 1) = 4 * (2/5)^(k - 1). Common ratio r = 2/5 = 0.4 < 1. Therefore, series D converges.
exam_questions.topic_name: Infinite Series - Convergence of Geometric Series

exam_questions.question_text: What is the area of a triangle with vertices A (0, 0), B (1, -3) and C (5, 1) (in square units)?
exam_questions.topic_name: Coordinate Geometry - Triangle Area by Coordinates

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following pairs of lines are perpendicular to each other?
exam_questions.option_a: y - x + 5 = 0 and y + x - 1 = 0
exam_questions.explanation: Line 1: y = x - 5 (slope m₁ = 1). Line 2: y = -x + 1 (slope m₂ = -1). Product of slopes: m₁ * m₂ = 1 * (-1) = -1. Therefore, the two lines in A are perpendicular.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following logarithmic equations is correctly related with the corresponding exponential equation?
exam_questions.option_a: log_a (x) = y and x^a = y
exam_questions.option_b: log_a (x) = y and aʸ = x
exam_questions.option_c: log_a (x) = y and xʸ = a
exam_questions.explanation: By mathematical definition of logarithms: log_a (x) = y is equivalent to the exponential form aʸ = x (with base a > 0, a ≠ 1, x > 0).

exam_questions.question_text: For any three sets A, B and C which one of the following is NOT true about the intersection of sets?
exam_questions.option_a: A ∩ B = A if A ⊆ B
exam_questions.option_b: A ∩ ∅ = A
exam_questions.option_c: A ∩ B = B ∩ A
options: A ∩ B = A if A ⊆ B
exam_questions.explanation: The intersection of any set with the empty set is always the empty set: A ∩ ∅ = ∅. Thus, statement B stating A ∩ ∅ = A is false (NOT true).

exam_questions.question_text: What is the major difference between practical geography and theoretical geography?
exam_questions.option_a: Practical geography studies the universe while theoretical studies only Earth.
exam_questions.option_b: Practical geography involves field work and applied techniques while theoretical focuses on concepts and models.
exam_questions.option_c: Theoretical geography uses field equipment while practical does not.
exam_questions.option_d: Practical geography is purely philosophical while theoretical is mathematical.
options: Practical geography studies the universe while theoretical studies only Earth.
Practical geography involves field work and applied techniques while theoretical focuses on concepts and models.
Theoretical geography uses field equipment while practical does not.
Practical geography is purely philosophical while theoretical is mathematical.
exam_questions.explanation: Theoretical geography deals with developing geographic concepts, laws, hypotheses, and spatial theories, whereas practical geography applies empirical methods, cartography, GIS, field surveying, and spatial analysis to solve real-world problems.

exam_questions.question_text: Which early Greek scholar is credited with coining the term 'Geography ' and calculating the Earth' s circumference with remarkable accuracy?
exam_questions.option_a: Hero dot us
exam_questions.option_b: Strabo
exam_questions.option_c: Ptolemy
exam_questions.explanation: Era tos thenes (c. 276–194 BC) was the chief librarian at Alexandria who coined the word 'Geographia' (earth description) and accurately computed the Earth's circumference using sun angles between Syene and Alexandria.

exam_questions.question_text: During which period did the 'Quantitative Revolution' transform geography into a spatial science using statistical and mathematical models?
exam_questions.option_a: Early 18th century
exam_questions.option_b: Mid-20th century (1950s - 1960s)
exam_questions.option_c: Late 19th century
exam_questions.explanation: The Quantitative Revolution in geography occur red during the 1950s and 1960s, shifting geography from descriptive regionalism to rigorous spatial analysis, statistical modeling, and scientific hypothesis testing.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Human Geography from Physical Geography?
exam_questions.option_a: Human geography studies atmospheric dynamics, whereas physical geography studies urban settlements.
exam_questions.option_b: Physical geography is concerned with cultural lands capes, while human geography studies land forms.
exam_questions.option_c: Human geography focuses on human societies and their spatial interactions, while physical geography investigates natural processes of the Earth.
exam_questions.option_d: There is no functional distinction between human and physical geography.
options: Human geography studies atmospheric dynamics, whereas physical geography studies urban settlements.
Physical geography is concerned with cultural landscapes, while human geography studies landforms.
Human geography focuses on human societies and their spatial interactions, while physical geography investigates natural processes of the Earth.
There is no functional distinction between human and physical geography.
exam_questions.explanation: Human geography investigates the patterns, processes, and spatial organization of human activities (population, culture, economics, urbanism), while physical geography studies the natural environment (lithosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere).

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is an essential marginal element of a standard map that defines the ratio between map distance and ground distance?
exam_questions.option_a: North arrow
exam_questions.option_b: Legend
exam_questions.option_c: Grid lines
exam_questions.explanation: Map scale mathematically expresses the relationship (ratio or proportion) between a given distance measured on the map and the corresponding real distance on the ground.

exam_questions.question_text: On a topographic map, individual features such as water wells, bench marks, and historical monuments are typically represented by:
exam_questions.option_a: Point symbols (dots/icons)
exam_questions.option_b: Line symbols
exam_questions.option_c: Area/Polygon symbols
exam_questions.explanation: Cartographic symbols are categorized into point, line, and area symbols. Point symbols represent zero-dimensional geographic locations with fixed coordinates, such as wells, church buildings, spot heights, and monuments.

exam_questions.question_text: If a map has a Represent ative Fraction (R. F.) scale of 1:50,000, what is the actual ground distance represented by a line measuring 4 cm on the map?
exam_questions.option_a: 2 kilometers
exam_questions.option_b: 20 kilometers
exam_questions.option_c: 200 meters
exam_questions.explanation: 1 cm on map = 50,000 cm on the ground = 500 meters = 0.5 km. Ground distance = 4 cm * 0.5 km/cm = 2.0 km.

exam_questions.question_text: When contour lines on a topographic map are spaced very close together, they indicate:
exam_questions.option_a: A steep slope
exam_questions.option_b: A gentle slope
exam_questions.option_c: A flat plain
exam_questions.explanation: Contour lines connect points of equal elevation. When contours are closely packed, elevation changes rapidly over a short horizontal distance, representing a steep slope or cliff.

exam_questions.question_text: A direction measured in degrees clock wise starting from True North (000° to 360°) is known as:
exam_questions.option_a: Magnetic declination
exam_questions.option_b: True bearing (Azimuth)
exam_questions.option_c: Grid coordinate
exam_questions.explanation: True bearing (whole circle azimuth) is the horizontal angle measured clock wise from True North (0°/360°) to a target line.

exam_questions.question_text: What does the acronym GIS stand for in modern geospatial technology?
exam_questions.option_a: Geological International Standard
exam_questions.option_b: Global Internet System
exam_questions.option_c: Geographic Information System
exam_questions.explanation: GIS stands for Geographic Information System, an integrated frame work for capturing, managing, analyzing, and displaying all forms of geographically referenced spatial and attribute data.

exam_questions.question_text: The science and art of gathering data about an object or surface without making physical contact, using sensors on satellites or aircraft, is called:
exam_questions.option_a: Cadastral surveying
exam_questions.option_b: Geodesy
exam_questions.option_c: Triangulation
exam_questions.explanation: Remote sensing is the acquisition of information about the Earth's surface and atmosphere from a distance, typically through electromagnetic radiation sensors mounted on satellites, aircraft, or drones.

exam_questions.question_text: Global Positioning System (GPS) determines exact geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude, altitude) by receiving signals from:
exam_questions.option_a: A constellation of Earth-orbiting satellites
exam_questions.option_b: Ground-based seismic stations
exam_questions.option_c: Atmospheric weather balloons
exam_questions.explanation: GPS functions by trilaterating radio signals transmitted from a constellation of or biting satellites (minimum 4 satellites in view) to compute precise 3D position coordinates and time.

exam_questions.question_text: The Earth's lithosphere is comprised of which structural layers?
exam_questions.option_a: The inner core and outer core
exam_questions.option_b: The crust and the upper most rigid part of the mantle
exam_questions.option_c: The asthenosphere and lower mantle
options: The inner core and outer core
The crust and the uppermost rigid part of the mantle
exam_questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the solid, rigid outer mechanical shell of the Earth, encompassing the entire crust (continental and oceanic) and the brittle upper most mantle, resting above the plastic asthenosphere.

exam_questions.question_text: The theory that describes the large-scale motion of seven major and numerous minor lithospheric plates over the asthenosphere is known as:
exam_questions.option_a: Geosynclinal theory
exam_questions.option_b: Isostasy
exam_questions.option_c: Plate Tectonics
exam_questions.explanation: Plate Tectonics is the unifying geological theory explaining continental drift, sea floor spreading, seismic activity, volcanism, and mountain building through the movement of tectonic plates.

exam_questions.question_text: Which geological feature is typically formed at divergent plate boundaries where tectonic plates pull apart?
exam_questions.option_a: Rift valleys and mid-ocean ridges
exam_questions.option_b: Deep ocean trenches
exam_questions.option_c: Fold mountains
exam_questions.explanation: At divergent (constructive) plate boundaries, extensional forces pull plates apart, creating continental rift valleys (e.g., East African Rift) and mid-ocean ridges (e.g., Mid-Atlantic Ridge) as magma rises to form new crust.

exam_questions.question_text: The mechanical disintegration and chemical decomposition of rocks in situ (without major transport) is defined as:
exam_questions.option_a: Erosion
exam_questions.option_b: Deposit i on
exam_questions.option_c: Mass wasting
exam_questions.explanation: Weathering is the breakdown of rocks, minerals, and soils in place (in situ) through atmospheric, chemical, and biological processes without significant transport.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following processes is a prime example of chemical weathering?
exam_questions.option_a: Frost wedging (freeze-thaw action)
exam_questions.option_b: Carbon ation and oxidation of rock minerals
exam_questions.option_c: Thermal expansion and contract i on
options: Carbonation and oxidation of rock minerals
exam_questions.explanation: Chemical weathering alters the chemical composition of rocks. Carbon ation (carbonic acid dissolving calcium carbonate in limestone) and oxidation (reaction of iron with oxygen) are prominent chemical weathering processes.

exam_questions.question_text: An oxbow lake is a crescent-shaped water body formed during the old age stage of a river by:
exam_questions.option_a: Glacial scouring of bed rock
exam_questions.option_b: Volcanic caldera collapse
exam_questions.option_c: River meander neck cut-off and deposit i on of alluvium
options: River meander neck cut-off and deposition of alluvium
exam_questions.explanation: As a mature meandering river flows across a flood plain, lateral erosion narrows the meander neck. During high floods, the river cuts through the neck directly, and alluvial deposit i on seals off the abandoned loop, forming an oxbow lake.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is a classic erosional land form created by alpine glaciation?
exam_questions.option_a: U-shaped valley (glacial trough)
exam_questions.option_b: V-shaped river valley
exam_questions.option_c: Barchan sand dune
exam_questions.explanation: Glaciers widen, deepen, and straighten pre-existing river valleys, transforming narrow V-shaped river valleys into steep-sided, flat-bottomed U-shaped valleys (glacial troughs).

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following land forms is produced by wind erosion (deflation and abrasion) in arid desert regions?
exam_questions.option_a: Drumlins and eskers
exam_questions.option_b: Yardangs and Zeugen
exam_questions.option_c: Sink holes and stalactites
exam_questions.explanation: Yardangs (elongated streamlined ridges) and Zeugen (tabular rock masses under cut by sand blasting) are distinctive erosional land forms created by wind abrasion and deflation in desert environments.

exam_questions.question_text: In which layer of the Earth's atmosphere is the ozone layer (O₃) concentrated, absorbing harmful ultraviolet (UV) solar radiation?
exam_questions.option_a: Troposphere
exam_questions.option_b: Stratosphere
exam_questions.option_c: Mesosphere
exam_questions.explanation: The ozone layer is located in the lower stratosphere (approximately 15 to 35 km above sea level), where it absorbs high-energy UV-B and UV-C solar radiation.

exam_questions.question_text: The natural atmospheric process that warms the Earth's lower atmosphere by absorbing and re-emitting terrestrial infrared radiation is called the:
exam_questions.option_a: Green house Effect
exam_questions.option_b: Coriolis effect
exam_questions.option_c: Adiabatic lapse rate
exam_questions.explanation: The green house effect occurs when atmospheric gases (water vapor, CO₂, CH₄, N₂O) absorb long-wave terrestrial infrared radiation emitted by the Earth, keeping global average surface temperatures hospitable for life.

exam_questions.question_text: As altitude (elevation) above sea level increases, what happens to atmospheric pressure?
exam_questions.option_a: Atmospheric pressure increases exponentially.
exam_questions.option_b: Atmospheric pressure decreases due to lower air column density.
exam_questions.option_c: Atmospheric pressure remains completely unchanged.
exam_questions.option_d: Atmospheric pressure fluctuates wildly with no relation to elevation.
options: Atmospheric pressure decreases due to lower air column density.
Atmospheric pressure fluctuates wildly with no relation to elevation.
exam_questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the overlying column of air per unit area. As altitude increases, fewer air molecules remain above, causing atmospheric pressure to decrease continuously with height.

exam_questions.question_text: Due to the Earth's rotation from west to east, the Coriolis force deflects moving winds and ocean currents:
exam_questions.option_a: To the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere
exam_questions.option_b: To the left in the Northern Hemisphere and to the right in the Southern Hemisphere
exam_questions.option_c: Straight towards the poles in both hemispheres
exam_questions.option_d: Straight towards the Equator in both hemispheres
options: To the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere
To the left in the Northern Hemisphere and to the right in the Southern Hemisphere
Straight towards the poles in both hemispheres
Straight towards the Equator in both hemispheres
exam_questions.explanation: Ferrel's Law states that because of the Coriolis effect, any freely moving object or fluid is deflected to the right of its path in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

exam_questions.question_text: What does the abbreviation ITCZ stand for in equatorial climatology?
exam_questions.option_a: International Temperature Control Zone
exam_questions.option_b: Inter-Continental Terrestrial Center
exam_questions.option_c: Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone
exam_questions.explanation: The ITCZ (Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone) is a broad low-pressure belt near the equator where the north east trade winds and south east trade winds converge, producing intense convectional rain fall.

exam_questions.question_text: Monsoon winds are fundamentally characterized by:
exam_questions.option_a: Constant velocity blowing continuously in a single direction throughout the entire year
exam_questions.option_b: A complete seasonal reversal in wind direction driven by differential heating of land and sea
exam_questions.option_c: Purely localized katabatic mountain breezes occur ring at night
exam_questions.option_d: Cold polar easterlies circulating only over ice caps
options: Constant velocity blowing continuously in a single direction throughout the entire year
A complete seasonal reversal in wind direction driven by differential heating of land and sea
Purely localized katabatic mountain breezes occurring at night
Cold polar easterlies circulating only over ice caps
exam_questions.explanation: Monsoons are large-scale seasonal wind systems characterized by a periodic reversal in prevailing wind direction, primarily caused by temperature and pressure differentials between vast continental land masses and adjacent oceans.

exam_questions.question_text: The global hydrological cycle is primarily powered by:
exam_questions.option_a: Earth's magnetic field and tectonic friction
exam_questions.option_b: Tidal friction from lunar gravity alone
exam_questions.option_c: Volcanic degassing and mantle convection
options: Earth's magnetic field and tectonic friction
Tidal friction from lunar gravity alone
exam_questions.explanation: The hydrological cycle is driven by solar radiation (which provides energy for evaporation and transpiration) and gravitational force (which causes condensation precipitation, run off, and percolation).

exam_questions.question_text: The gently sloping, relatively shallow submerged margin of a continent extending from the coast to the continental slope is called the:
exam_questions.option_a: Continental shelf
exam_questions.option_b: Abyssal plain
exam_questions.option_c: Ocean trench
exam_questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the shallow under water edge of a continental land mass, averaging less than 200 meters in depth, rich in marine life and off shore mineral/petroleum resources.

exam_questions.question_text: How do warm ocean currents influence the climate of adjacent coastal regions?
exam_questions.option_a: They create arid coastal deserts with extreme fog.
exam_questions.option_b: They lower air temperatures and reduce atmospheric moisture.
exam_questions.option_c: They raise coastal air temperatures and increase precipitation and humidity.
exam_questions.option_d: They cause perpetual sub-zero freezing along tropical shore lines.
options: They create arid coastal deserts with extreme fog.
They lower air temperatures and reduce atmospheric moisture.
They raise coastal air temperatures and increase precipitation and humidity.
They cause perpetual sub-zero freezing along tropical shorelines.
exam_questions.explanation: Warm ocean currents heat the overlying maritime air, boosting evaporation and atmospheric moisture, which leads to higher temperatures and increased rain fall on adjacent coastal lands.

exam_questions.question_text: The periodic climatic phenomenon characterized by abnormal warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean is known as:
exam_questions.option_a: El Niño (ENSO)
exam_questions.option_b: La Niña
exam_questions.option_c: Benguela Current
exam_questions.explanation: El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), characterized by unusual warming of surface waters in the eastern tropical Pacific, disrupting global atmospheric circulation and causing severe droughts or floods world wide.

exam_questions.question_text: According to soil science, which five interrelated factors determine soil formation (pedogenesis)?
exam_questions.option_a: Magnetism, sun light, ocean tides, wind speed, latitude
exam_questions.option_b: Bed rock hardness, earthquakes, tectonic drift, volcanic ash, glaciers
exam_questions.option_c: Human settlement, industrialization, crop rotation, fertilization, irrigation
exam_questions.option_d: Parent material, climate, living organisms, topography/relief, and time (CLORPT)
options: Magnetism, sunlight, ocean tides, wind speed, latitude
Bedrock hardness, earthquakes, tectonic drift, volcanic ash, glaciers
Human settlement, industrialization, crop rotation, fertilization, irrigation
Parent material, climate, living organisms, topography/relief, and time (CLORPT)
exam_questions.explanation: Hans Jenny's foundational soil equation identifies five primary soil-forming factors: Climate, Organisms, Relief (topography), Parent material, and Time (CLORPT).

exam_questions.question_text: In a typical soil profile, which upper most horizon contains the highest concentration of decomposed organic matter (humus) and biological activity?
exam_questions.option_a: A horizon (Top soil) / O horizon
exam_questions.option_b: B horizon (Subsoil)
exam_questions.option_c: C horizon (Weathered parent rock)
exam_questions.explanation: The O (organic) and A (top soil) horizons sit at the top of the soil profile, rich in decomposed humus, soil microorganisms, plant roots, and essential plant nutrients.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following agricultural practices is widely employed on steep slopes to control surface run off and prevent soil erosion?
exam_questions.option_a: Up-and-down slope plowing
exam_questions.option_b: Terracing and contour plowing
exam_questions.option_c: Overgrazing and monoculture
exam_questions.explanation: Contour plowing (plowing across slopes along contour lines) and terracing (creating stepped flat platforms) significantly reduce run off velocity, promoting water infiltration and preventing severe soil erosion.

exam_questions.question_text: The tropical rain forest biome (selva) is distinguished by which combination of environmental characteristics?
exam_questions.option_a: Year-round high temperatures, heavy rain fall, multi-layered dense canopy, and high biodiversity
exam_questions.option_b: Extremely dry conditions, sparse cacti, extreme daily temperature range
exam_questions.option_c: Severe sub-zero winters, coniferous pine forests, low annual precipitation
exam_questions.option_d: Treeless grass lands with continuous permafrost
options: Year-round high temperatures, heavy rainfall, multi-layered dense canopy, and high biodiversity
Extremely dry conditions, sparse cacti, extreme daily temperature range
Severe sub-zero winters, coniferous pine forests, low annual precipitation
exam_questions.explanation: Tropical rain forest biomes (found along equatorial basins such as the Amazon and Congo) feature high annual temperatures (>24°C), abundant annual rain fall (>2000 mm), stratified multi-canopy ever green trees, and Earth's highest terrestrial biodiversity.
exam_questions.topic_name: Biomes of the World - Tropical Rainforest

exam_questions.question_text: The Savanna biome is best described as:
exam_questions.option_a: An ever green boreal forest dominated by spruce and fir trees
exam_questions.option_b: A frozen desert devoid of vegetative life
exam_questions.option_c: A tropical grass land ecosystem with scattered drought-resistant trees, experiencing distinct wet and dry seasons
exam_questions.option_d: A temperate deciduous forest with high snow fall in winter
options: An evergreen boreal forest dominated by spruce and fir trees
A frozen desert devoid of vegetative life
A tropical grassland ecosystem with scattered drought-resistant trees, experiencing distinct wet and dry seasons
A temperate deciduous forest with high snowfall in winter
exam_questions.explanation: Savannas are tropical grass land biomes found between tropical wet and semi-arid zones, characterized by tall grasses, scattered acacia and baobab trees, and pronounced wet and dry seasons.

exam_questions.question_text: Which terrestrial biome is characterized by permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost), short cool summers, and low-growing vegetation such as mosses and lichens?
exam_questions.option_a: Taiga
exam_questions.option_b: Tundra
exam_questions.option_c: Chaparral
exam_questions.explanation: The Arctic and Alpine Tundra biomes are characterized by permafrost, extreme cold, short growing seasons, and dwarf vegetation (lichens, mosses, small sedges).

exam_questions.question_text: A biogeographic region characterized by exceptionally high levels of endemic species that is simultaneously under severe threat of habit at destruction is termed a:
exam_questions.option_a: Biosphere transition zone
exam_questions.option_b: Microclimate envelope
exam_questions.option_c: Monoculture corridor
