options: palisade mesophyll ,upper epidermis ,lower epidermis and guard cells
Upper epidermis ,palisade mesophyll, lower epidermis and guard cells
Upper epidermis ,palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll and stomata
Upper epidermis ,palisade mesophyll, lower epidermis and guard cells
exam_questions.explanation: In a typical leaf cross section: 1 represents the upper epidermis (covered by cuticle), 2 represents the vertically elongated palisade mesophyll containing abundant chloroplasts, 3 is the vascular bundle (xylem/phloem), 4 is the lower epidermis, 5 is spongy mesophyll, and 6 represents the guard cells surrounding the stomatal pore.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The high concentration of auxin will be on lower side of both shoot and root when a seedling placed horizontally, however growth direction of shoot and root is not similar. This is because :
exam_questions.option_a: The high concentration of auxin promote growth of both shoot and root
exam_questions.option_b: The high concentration of auxin which promote growth of shoot inhibit growth of root
exam_questions.option_c: The low concentration of auxin in lower side inhibit growth of shoot and root
exam_questions.option_d: The low concentration of auxin promote growth of shoot but inhibit growth of root
options: The high concentration of auxin promote growth of both shoot and root
The high concentration of auxin which promote growth of shoot inhibit growth of root
The low concentration of auxin in lower side inhibit growth of shoot and root
The low concentration of auxin promote growth of shoot but inhibit growth of root
exam_questions.explanation: Shoots and roots have different sensitivity to auxin. High auxin concentration on the lower side promotes cell elongation in the shoot (causing it to curve upward, negative gravitropism), but inhibits cell elongation in the root (causing the upper side to grow faster and curve downward, positive gravitropism).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following alternative contains the structure of leaf which is correctly matched its function
exam_questions.option_a: Waxy cuticle -allows diffusion of gases in and out of leaf
exam_questions.option_b: Guard cells - provide big surface area for gas exchange
exam_questions.option_c: Palisade mesophyll -main photosynthetic tissues of leaf
exam_questions.option_d: Spongy mesophyll controls opening & closing of stomata
options: Waxy cuticle -allows diffusion of gases in and out of leaf
Guard cells - provide big surface area for gas exchange
Palisade mesophyll -main photosynthetic tissues of leaf
Spongy mesophyll controls opening & closing of stomata
exam_questions.explanation: The palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts and positioned perpendicular to the upper leaf surface to maximize light interception, serving as the main site of photosynthesis in leaves.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of the process taken place in hypogeal germination?
exam_questions.option_a: Hypocotyl is elongated and bringing the cotyledon above the ground
exam_questions.option_b: Epicotyl is elongated and bringing the cotyledon above the ground
exam_questions.option_c: Epicotyl is elongated and leaving the cotyledon below the ground
exam_questions.option_d: Hypocotyl is elongated and leaving the cotyledon below the ground
options: Hypocotyl is elongated and bringing the cotyledon above the ground
Epicotyl is elongated and bringing the cotyledon above the ground
Epicotyl is elongated and leaving the cotyledon below the ground
Hypocotyl is elongated and leaving the cotyledon below the ground
exam_questions.explanation: In hypogeal germination (e.g., in maize and broad beans), the epicotyl rapidly elongates while the hypocotyl remains short, pushing the plumule upward while leaving the cotyledons buried beneath the soil surface.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is not involved in light dependent stage of photosynthesis?
exam_questions.option_a: Formation of ATP
exam_questions.option_b: Oxidation of NADPH2 to NADP+
exam_questions.option_c: Photolysis of water
exam_questions.explanation: In the light-dependent reactions (occur ring in thylakoid membranes), water is split (photolysis), releasing O2, and NADP+ is reduced to NADPH while ATP is generated via photophosphorylation. Oxidation of NADPH back to NADP+ occurs in the light-independent Calvin cycle (stroma).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statement about xylem is true?
exam_questions.option_a: It is living tissue absorb water and mineral from soil
exam_questions.option_b: It is made up of dead tissue which transport the product of photosynthesis
exam_questions.option_c: It is made up of living tissue which transport product of photosynthesis
exam_questions.option_d: it is made up of dead tissue which transport water and minerals from root to the leaves
options: It is living tissue absorb water and mineral from soil
It is made up of dead tissue which transport the product of photosynthesis
It is made up of living tissue which transport product of photosynthesis
it is made up of dead tissue which transport water and minerals from root to the leaves
exam_questions.explanation: Mature xylem vessels and tracheids are dead, hollow, lignified tubes that conduct water and dissolved inorganic minerals uni direction ally from roots up to leaves.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is not true about tropism?
exam_questions.option_a: Shoot is positively phototropic but root is negatively phototropic
exam_questions.option_b: Root is positively hydrotropic but shoot is negatively hydrotropic
exam_questions.option_c: Shoot is positively geotropic but root is negatively geotropic
exam_questions.option_d: Root is positively Gravitropic and shoot is negatively Gravitropic
options: Shoot is positively phototropic but root is negatively phototropic
Root is positively hydrotropic but shoot is negatively hydrotropic
Shoot is positively geotropic but root is negatively geotropic
Root is positively Gravitropic and shoot is negatively Gravitropic
exam_questions.explanation: Shoots grow away from gravity (negatively geotropic / gravitropic) while roots grow toward gravity into the soil (positively geotropic / gravitropic). Therefore, claiming shoots are positively geotropic is false.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of photosynthesis?
exam_questions.option_a: Light reaction stage is takes place in stroma
exam_questions.option_b: Carbondioxide is fixed in dark reaction
exam_questions.option_c: Dark reaction is involved only during night time
exam_questions.option_d: Light independent stage is involved in grana of chloroplast
options: Light reaction stage is takes place in stroma
Carbondioxide is fixed in dark reaction
Dark reaction is involved only during night time
Light independent stage is involved in grana of chloroplast
exam_questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide fix ation occurs during the light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle / dark reactions) in the stroma of the chloroplast, catalyzed by the enzyme RuBisCO.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Select the one that characterizes higher plants
exam_questions.option_a: They are sessile
exam_questions.option_b: They are mobile
exam_questions.option_c: They have fragile cell wall
exam_questions.explanation: Higher plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) are stationary (sessile) organisms anchored to a substrate by root systems, possessing rigid cell walls made of cellulose and lignin.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: What is the implication of seed dispersal?
exam_questions.option_a: Diversify plants
exam_questions.option_b: Increase competition for light
exam_questions.option_c: Doesn't have implication for colonization of new niches
exam_questions.option_d: Seed dispersal is not important in plant reproduction
options: Doesn't have implication for colonization of new niches
Seed dispersal is not important in plant reproduction
exam_questions.explanation: Seed dispersal allows plants to colonize new geographic areas, avoid intense intraspecific competition near parent plants, and spread genetic diversity across wider ecological ranges.

exam_questions.question_text: Answer the following question based on the biochemical food test table: Iodine confirms positive for Potato; Benedict's confirms positive for Honey; Ethanol emulsion confirms positive for Cooking oil; Biuret reagent confirms positive for Egg albumin. Which statement is incorrect about the biochemical food test indicated?
exam_questions.option_a: Adding Iodine solution confirms for starch presence in the potato.
exam_questions.option_b: Boiling Benedict solution confirms presence of non-reducing sugar in honey.
exam_questions.option_c: Mixing ethanol with cooking oil confirms lipid is insoluble in water
exam_questions.option_d: Adding Biuret reagent confirm protein presence in egg albumin.
options: Adding Iodine solution confirms for starch presence in the potato.
Boiling Benedict solution confirms presence of non-reducing sugar in honey.
Mixing ethanol with cooking oil confirms lipid is insoluble in water
Adding Biuret reagent confirm protein presence in egg albumin.
exam_questions.explanation: Benedict's solution detects REDUCING sugars (such as glucose and fructose, which are abundant in honey), not non-reducing sugars. Non-reducing sugars (like sucrose) give a negative Benedict's test unless first hydrolyzed with acid.

exam_questions.question_text: If you visit water bodies like river and lake you can find some organisms walk on the water surface. What conclusion you would give concerning the characteristics of water which allow those organisms move on water?
exam_questions.option_a: High latent heat of vaporization
exam_questions.option_b: Boiling and freezing point
exam_questions.option_c: Density and freezing properties
exam_questions.explanation: Water has high surface tension due to the strong cohesive hydrogen bonding between water molecules at the air-water interface, creating a film-like elastic surface capable of supporting light insects like water striders.
exam_questions.topic_name: Properties of Water in Biological Systems
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Choose the letter that contains only macronutrients?
exam_questions.option_a: Sodium, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus
exam_questions.option_b: Phosphorus, manganese, iron and copper
exam_questions.option_c: Magnesium, manganese, iron and potassium
exam_questions.explanation: Macronutrients are required by organisms in relatively large quantities. Sodium (Na), potassium (K), magnesium (Mg), and phosphorus (P) are essential macronutrients. Iron, copper, and manganese are micronutrients (trace elements).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of characteristics of water and its importance in life?
exam_questions.option_a: Cohesive and adhesive force- transport of water from the root to the leaves of the plants
exam_questions.option_b: Water as solvent- involved in condensation reaction to make polymer
exam_questions.option_c: Boiling and freezing point- sustain aquatic ecosystem & regulate body temperature
exam_questions.option_d: Unique density and freezing point - Increase survival rate of life under cold temperature
options: Cohesive and adhesive force- transport of water from the root to the leaves of the plants
Water as solvent- involved in condensation reaction to make polymer
Boiling and freezing point- sustain aquatic ecosystem & regulate body temperature
Unique density and freezing point - Increase survival rate of life under cold temperature
exam_questions.explanation: Cohesion (hydrogen bonding between water molecules) and adhesion (attraction between water molecules and xylem walls) drive the continuous transpiration stream pulling water from roots up to leaves.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is not true clinical condition caused by inorganic ions through alteration of its usual concentration?
exam_questions.option_a: Wilson disease is caused by abnormal copper deposit i on in liver and brain
exam_questions.option_b: Increase in take of sodium result in high blood pressure
exam_questions.option_c: Abnormal iron deposit i on causes hemochromatosis
options: Wilson disease is caused by abnormal copper deposition in liver and brain
Increase in take of sodium result in high blood pressure
exam_questions.explanation: While iodine deficiency can cause goiter, goiter itself is an enlargement of the thyroid gland resulting from thyroid dysregulation (which can be associated with hypothyroidism), but between the clinical choices, mineral ion disorders are: Wilson's (Cu), Hypertension (Na), Hemochromatosis (Fe), whereas goiter is primarily caused by dietary iodine deficiency leading to elevated TSH.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: As a biology student what you recommend for our community to prevent spread of goiter?
exam_questions.option_a: Taking excess amount of iodine rich food like dairy products.
exam_questions.option_b: Create awareness on eating of iodized salt
exam_questions.option_c: Removing of enlarged thyroid gland which cause deformity
exam_questions.option_d: Adding of leguminous plant such as bean and pea in daily diet
options: Taking excess amount of iodine rich food like dairy products.
Create awareness on eating of iodized salt
Removing of enlarged thyroid gland which cause deformity
Adding of leguminous plant such as bean and pea in daily diet
exam_questions.explanation: The most effective and sustainable public health intervention to prevent endemic goiter and iodine deficiency disorders (IDD) is promoting the consumption of universal iodized salt in the daily diet.

exam_questions.question_text: There are 20 different amino acids in nature which make up different types of proteins. What makes one amino acid different from another?
exam_questions.option_a: Different carboxyl groups attached to carbon
exam_questions.option_b: Different amino groups attached to carbon
exam_questions.option_c: Different side chains attached to carbon
options: Different carboxyl groups attached to carbon
Different amino groups attached to carbon
Different side chains attached to carbon
exam_questions.explanation: All amino acids share a common central alpha-carbon bonded to a hydrogen atom, an amino group (-NH2), and a carboxyl group (-COOH). They differ from one another exclusively by their specific chemical side chain (the variable 'R' group).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of fibrous proteins?
exam_questions.option_a: Enzymes
exam_questions.option_b: Keratin
exam_questions.option_c: Antibodies
exam_questions.explanation: Keratin, collagen, and elastin are insoluble, elongated fibrous structural proteins that provide mechanical support and protection in hair, nails, skin, and tend ons. Enzymes, antibodies, and hemoglobin are globular proteins.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text:
Which of the following represent the type of complex carbohydrates, RESPECTIVELY:
I. carbohydrate storage in animal liver
II. structural component of plant cell walls
III. carbohydrate storage in plants
IV. Exoskeleton of insects
exam_questions.option_a: Glycogen, Starch, Chitin, Cellulose
exam_questions.option_b: Glycogen, Chitin, Starch, Cellulose
exam_questions.option_c: Glycogen, Starch, Cellulose, Chitin
exam_questions.explanation: I = Glycogen (animal storage), II = Cellulose (plant cell walls), III = Starch (plant storage), and IV = Chitin (arthropod exoskeleton and fungal cell walls).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The molecular formula for glucose is C6H12O6. What would be the molecular formula for a molecule made by linking three glucose molecules together by condensation reactions?
exam_questions.explanation:
Linking 3 glucose molecules involves 2 condensation reactions, each eliminating one water molecule (H2O):
Formula = 3 × (C6H12O6) - 2 × (H2O) = C18H36O18 - H4O2 = C18H32O16.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Phospholipids are group of lipids which are made up of:
exam_questions.option_a: One glycerol, one fatty acid & two phosphate groups.
exam_questions.option_b: One glycerol, two fatty acids & a phosphate group
exam_questions.option_c: One glycerol, three fatty acids & a phosphate group.
exam_questions.option_d: One glycerol, two fatty acids & two phosphate groups.
options: One glycerol, one fatty acid & two phosphate groups.
One glycerol, two fatty acids & a phosphate group
One glycerol, three fatty acids & a phosphate group.
One glycerol, two fatty acids & two phosphate groups.
exam_questions.explanation: A phospholipid consists of a glycerol back bone esterified to two nonpolar hydrophobic fatty acid chains and one polar hydrophilic phosphate group (often attached to a choline or other head group).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: All of the following statements concerning saturated fats are true EXCEPT
exam_questions.option_a: They are more common in animals than in plants.
exam_questions.option_b: They generally solidify at room temperature.
exam_questions.option_c: They have multiple double bonds in the carbon chains of their fatty acids.
exam_questions.option_d: They contain more hydrogen than unsaturated fats
options: They are more common in animals than in plants.
They generally solidify at room temperature.
They have multiple double bonds in the carbon chains of their fatty acids.
They contain more hydrogen than unsaturated fats
exam_questions.explanation: Saturated fats have NO double bonds (C=C) in their hydrocarbon fatty acid chains; they are fully 'saturated' with hydrogen atoms, allowing them to pack closely and remain solid at room temperature.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is true regarding the chemical reaction illustrated in the figure (showing two amino acids joining with the removal of H2O)?
exam_questions.option_a: It is a hydrolysis reaction.
exam_questions.option_b: It results in a peptide bond.
exam_questions.option_c: It joins two fatty acids together
exam_questions.option_d: It results in a glycosidic bond
options: It results in a peptide bond.
It joins two fatty acids together
It results in a glycosidic bond
exam_questions.explanation: The reaction shows condensation (dehydration synthesis) between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of an adjacent amino acid, releasing water (H2O) and forming a covalent peptide bond (-CO-NH-).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statement concerning description of G1 stage of cell cycle is true?
exam_questions.option_a: Cells are quite active metabolically, accumulate building blocks of DNA and associated protein
exam_questions.option_b: It is a stage at which DNA is replicated and make final preparation before it undergoes mitosis
exam_questions.option_c: Is the stage when cell replenish its energy store and synthesize protein necessary for chromosome manipulation and movement.
exam_questions.option_d: It is the stage at which nucleus and cytoplasm divides and produce two daughter cells
options: Cells are quite active metabolically, accumulate building blocks of DNA and associated protein
It is a stage at which DNA is replicated and make final preparation before it undergoes mitosis
Is the stage when cell replenish its energy store and synthesize protein necessary for chromosome manipulation and movement.
It is the stage at which nucleus and cytoplasm divides and produce two daughter cells
exam_questions.explanation: During the G1 (first gap) phase of interphase, the cell undergoes vigorous metabolic activity, protein synthesis, and growth, accumulating the necessary nucleotide building blocks and enzymes needed for DNA replication in the S phase.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The cells produced in mitosis will have a:
exam_questions.option_a: Haploid number of chromosomes and will be genetically identical to each other.
exam_questions.option_b: Diploid number of chromosomes and will differ genetically from each other.
exam_questions.option_c: Diploid number of chromosomes and will be genetically identical to each other.
exam_questions.option_d: Haploid number of chromosomes and will differ genetically from each other
options: Haploid number of chromosomes and will be genetically identical to each other.
Diploid number of chromosomes and will differ genetically from each other.
Diploid number of chromosomes and will be genetically identical to each other.
Haploid number of chromosomes and will differ genetically from each other
exam_questions.explanation: Mitosis is an equational division resulting in two daughter cells that have the same diploid (2n) chromosome number and are genetically identical clones of the parent cell and each other.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The diagram below shows the stages of mitosis (A: Telophase/Cytokinesis, B: Prophase, C: Metaphase, D: An a phase). Which are correct sequences of these stages?
exam_questions.option_a: B, C, D, A
exam_questions.option_b: C, B, D, A
exam_questions.option_c: B, C, A, D
exam_questions.explanation: The chronological sequence of mitotic stages is: Prophase (B) -> Metaphase (C) -> An a phase (D) -> Telophase/Cytokinesis (A), which is B, C, D, A.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The difference between the sugar in DNA and the sugar in RNA is that the sugar in DNA
exam_questions.option_a: Contains one less oxygen atom.
exam_questions.option_b: Can form a double-stranded molecule.
exam_questions.option_c: Has a six-membered ring of carbon and nitrogen atom
exam_questions.option_d: Is a six-carbon sugar and the sugar in RNA is a five-carbon sugar.
options: Has a six-membered ring of carbon and nitrogen atom
Is a six-carbon sugar and the sugar in RNA is a five-carbon sugar.
exam_questions.explanation: Deoxyribose (in DNA, C5H10O4) lacks an oxygen atom at the 2' carbon position compared to ribose (in RNA, C5H10O5), which possesses a 2'-OH hydroxyl group.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: What are three components of RNA molecule?
exam_questions.option_a: Ribose sugar, a phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
exam_questions.option_b: Deoxy ribose sugar, a phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
exam_questions.option_c: Hexose sugar, a phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
exam_questions.option_d: A pentose sugar, two phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
options: Ribose sugar, a phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
Deoxy ribose sugar, a phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
Hexose sugar, a phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
A pentose sugar, two phosphate group & nitrogenous base.
exam_questions.explanation: An RNA nucleotide consists of three fundamental chemical components: a five-carbon ribose sugar, an inorganic phosphate group, and one of four nitrogenous bases (Adenine, Uracil, Cytosine, or Guanine).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following alternatives contain the incorrect association in stage of mitotic cell division?
exam_questions.option_a: Metaphase- Chromatids attached to the spindle fiber
exam_questions.option_b: Anaphase- Chromatids move to opposite poles of the cell
exam_questions.option_c: Telophase –Mitotic spindle breaks down and disappears
exam_questions.option_d: Prophase- chromosomes line up end to end along the metaphase plate
options: Metaphase- Chromatids attached to the spindle fiber
Anaphase- Chromatids move to opposite poles of the cell
Telophase –Mitotic spindle breaks down and disappears
Prophase- chromosomes line up end to end along the metaphase plate
exam_questions.explanation: Chromosomes line up along the equatorial metaphase plate during Metaphase, not Prophase. During Prophase, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, nucleoli disappear, and the mitotic spindle forms.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: A cell having 64 chromosomes (2n) undergoes mitotic cell division. then it results in
exam_questions.option_a: 2 daughter cells each with 32 chromosomes
exam_questions.option_b: 4 daughter cells each with 32 chromosomes
exam_questions.option_c: 4daughter cells each with 64 chromosomes
exam_questions.explanation: Mitosis yields exactly 2 daughter cells, and each daughter cell preserves the original diploid chromosome number (2n = 64 chromosomes).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the function of mitosis is false?
exam_questions.option_a: It allows organisms to generate genetic diversity.
exam_questions.option_b: It allows organisms to reproduce asexually.
exam_questions.option_c: It allows organisms to repair tissues.
options: It allows organisms to generate genetic diversity.
It allows organisms to reproduce asexually.
It allows organisms to repair tissues.
exam_questions.explanation: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells, preserving genetic constancy. Genetic diversity is generated by meiosis through crossing over (homologous recombination) and independent as sortment of chromosomes.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The tail of phospholipids molecules that make up cell membrane is:
exam_questions.option_a: Polar and water repellent
exam_questions.option_b: Polar and hydrophilic
exam_questions.option_c: Non-polar & water repellent
exam_questions.explanation: Phospholipid molecules are amphipathic: the phosphate head is polar and hydrophilic (water-loving), while the fatty acid hydrocarbon tails are non-polar and hydrophobic (water-repellent).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: How is the water in the xylem transport upwards to the top of the plant?
exam_questions.option_a: By pulling of transpiration stream
exam_questions.option_b: Due to high concentration of water in the soil
exam_questions.option_c: By using of cellular energy
options: Due to high concentration of water in the soil
exam_questions.explanation: Water is transported upward through xylem vessels mainly by the transpiration pull (transpiration stream), supported by the cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls (the Dixon and Joly cohesion-tension mechanism).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: In experiment with plant growth, scientists have found the plant tip will bend toward light this is because:
exam_questions.option_a: More Auxin will be in light side than dark side
exam_questions.option_b: Growth will more in dark side than illuminated side
exam_questions.option_c: Growth will more in illuminated side than dark side
exam_questions.option_d: Auxin moves towards light from dark side
options: More Auxin will be in light side than dark side
Growth will more in dark side than illuminated side
Growth will more in illuminated side than dark side
Auxin moves towards light from dark side
exam_questions.explanation: Light causes auxin to migrate to the shaded (dark) side of the shoot tip. The higher auxin concentration stimulates faster cell elongation on the dark side, bending the stem toward the light source (positive phototropism).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following internal structure of root is mismatched with its function?
exam_questions.option_a: Cortex – provide storage of food and water
exam_questions.option_b: Endodermis – Helps the movement of water and dissolved nutrients
exam_questions.option_c: Pericyle – The site of origin of lateral buds
exam_questions.option_d: Peliferous layer- composed of cuticles for water proof
options: Cortex – provide storage of food and water
Endodermis – Helps the movement of water and dissolved nutrients
Pericyle – The site of origin of lateral buds
Peliferous layer- composed of cuticles for waterproof
exam_questions.explanation: The piliferous (epiblema) layer of roots is responsible for water and mineral absorption and bears root hairs; it lacks a water proof waxy cuticle because a cuticle would obstruct the inward absorption of water from the soil.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Both types of nucleic acids are made from structures called nucleotide, however:
exam_questions.option_a: DNA is made from a single polynucleotide chain.
exam_questions.option_b: RNA is made from two polynucleotide chains.
exam_questions.option_c: RNA is much larger than DNA.
options: DNA is made from a single polynucleotide chain.
RNA is made from two polynucleotide chains.
RNA is much larger than DNA.
exam_questions.explanation: DNA typically exists as a stable, double-stranded antiparallel double helix, whereas RNA is predominantly a single-stranded polynucleotide chain.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following leaf structure is the most external part?
exam_questions.option_a: Palisade cell
exam_questions.option_b: Upper epidermis
exam_questions.option_c: Cuticle
exam_questions.explanation: The waxy cuticle is a non-cellular, hydrophobic outer layer secreted by epidermal cells that covers the outermost surface of the leaf to minimize transpiration.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Where in the plant cell does actual synthesis of sugar occur?
exam_questions.option_a: Matrix
exam_questions.option_b: Stroma
exam_questions.option_c: Granum
exam_questions.explanation: The synthesis of sugar (G3P/glucose) occurs in the stroma of the chloroplast, where the soluble enzymes of the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) utilize ATP and NADPH to reduce CO2 into carbohydrates.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text:
Choose the correct sentence made out of the given jumbled words:
'get usually I late up week ends on.'

exam_questions.option_b: I get up late on week ends usually.
exam_questions.option_c: Get up late on week ends I usually.
exam_questions.option_d: On week ends usually I get up late.
options: I usually get up late on weekends.
I get up late on weekends usually.
Get up late on weekends I usually.
On weekends usually I get up late.
exam_questions.explanation: In standard English sentence structure, adverbs of frequency like 'usually' precede the main verb ('get up') and time prepositional phrases ('on week ends') are placed at the end: Subject (I) + Adverb of frequency (usually) + Verb phrase (get up late) + Time phrase (on week ends).
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text:

exam_questions.option_c: The agent with whom I spoke was able to help me.
exam_questions.option_d: The agent whom with I spoke was able to help me.
options: I spoke the agent with whom was able to help me.
With the agent whom I spoke was able to help me.
The agent with whom I spoke was able to help me.
The agent whom with I spoke was able to help me.
exam_questions.explanation: 'The agent with whom I spoke was able to help me' correctly forms the complex sentence with a prepositional relative clause: 'The agent' (subject) + 'with whom I spoke' (relative clause with fronted preposition) + 'was able to help me' (predicate).

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is most likely taken from DESCRIPTIVE writing?

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is most likely taken from a NARRATIVE writing?

exam_questions.question_text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following sentences is a simple sentence?

exam_questions.reading_passage: My grand father Agbefia, was a wealthy fisherman. He owned four large drag-nets, a net thrown through a river to trap fish, and three fishing boats. He did not employ people, but he was the head of a fishing company. A group of men in the village where he lived helped him fishing, and in return they received a proportion of the catch, which their wives sold in the market, but they had no shares in the nets or boats. Every morning, this old man would leave his house before dawn and walk on the sea-shore. He watched the changing colors of the sea and studied the movement of the clouds in the sky. From these he foretold the fishing of that day. Many of his workers slept on to sea shore, and when he had his decision, he would wake them and give them their instruction before he turned to his house. He was also the chief's linguist. He had to attend the chief on all important occasion and to speak for him. My grand father was out standing and aw-inspiring figure as, dressed in his hand-woven brightly colored Kente, the cultural closing, with his golden linguists' staff in land, he conveyed to the people the wish of their chief. My grand mother, on the other hand, was not aw-inspiring at all. She was short and fat; her skin was the color of bronze; she laughed easily, and she did her best to shield me, and all the children of the house from the trouble that came our way. We called her " Mamadze " which means " Red grand mother " because of her coloring. During my childhood, my grand father had four wives and between them they had twenty-five children. He had had in all, eight wives, but the other four had proved disloyal, or in some other way unsatisfactory, and he had sent them away. My own grand mother, Yakuvi, was his favorite and the one who stayed with him to the term ination of his life. In middle age, my grand father built a small, but strong and attractive house, a few hundred yards away from the great family house and a compound, which was by then teeming with his children and grand children. And he took only my grand mother Yakuvi with him, and lived in peace there. During their last days, he married her for a second time in Christian ceremony.

exam_questions.reading_passage: My grand father Agbefia, was a wealthy fisherman. He owned four large drag-nets, a net thrown through a river to trap fish, and three fishing boats. He did not employ people, but he was the head of a fishing company. A group of men in the village where he lived helped him fishing, and in return they received a proportion of the catch, which their wives sold in the market, but they had no shares in the nets or boats. Every morning, this old man would leave his house before dawn and walk on the sea-shore. He watched the changing colors of the sea and studied the movement of the clouds in the sky. From these he foretold the fishing of that day. Many of his workers slept on to sea shore, and when he had his decision, he would wake them and give them their instruction before he turned to his house. He was also the chief's linguist. He had to attend the chief on all important occasion and to speak for him. My grand father was out standing and aw-inspiring figure as, dressed in his hand-woven brightly colored Kente, the cultural closing, with his golden linguists' staff in land, he conveyed to the people the wish of their chief. My grand mother, on the other hand, was not aw-inspiring at all. She was short and fat; her skin was the color of bronze; she laughed easily, and she did her best to shield me, and all the children of the house from the trouble that came our way. We called her " Mamadze " which means " Red grand mother " because of her coloring. During my childhood, my grand father had four wives and between them they had twenty-five children. He had had in all, eight wives, but the other four had proved disloyal, or in some other way unsatisfactory, and he had sent them away. My own grand mother, Yakuvi, was his favorite and the one who stayed with him to the term ination of his life. In middle age, my grand father built a small, but strong and attractive house, a few hundred yards away from the great family house and a compound, which was by then teeming with his children and grand children. And he took only my grand mother Yakuvi with him, and lived in peace there. During their last days, he married her for a second time in Christian ceremony.

exam_questions.question_text: If p (x) = 6x³ + 5x² - 3x + 2, then find the value of p(-1).
exam_questions.explanation:
Substitute x = -1 into the polynomial expression:
p(-1) = 6(-1)³ + 5(-1)² - 3(-1) + 2
= 6(-1) + 5 (1) + 3 + 2
= -6 + 5 + 3 + 2 = 4.

exam_questions.question_text: If f (x) = x³ - 2bx² + 16 is divisible by x + 2, then which one of the following is the value of b?
exam_questions.explanation:
By the Remainder/Factor Theorem, if f (x) is divisible by (x + 2), then f(-2) = 0:
f(-2) = (-2)³ - 2b(-2)² + 16 = 0
-8 - 2b (4) + 16 = 0
-8 - 8b + 16 = 0
8 - 8b = 0 => 8b = 8 => b = 1.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the degree of the polynomial function f (x) = (3x - 5)⁸(2x + 1)⁴?
exam_questions.explanation: The degree of a product of polynomials is the sum of the degrees of the individual factors. Degree of (3x - 5)⁸ is 8, and degree of (2x + 1)⁴ is 4. Total degree = 8 + 4 = 12.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the remainder when f (x) = 3x⁴ - 2x³ - 5x² + 6 is divided by x² - 1?

f (x) = 3 (x²)² - 2x (x²) - 5 (x²) + 6
Substituting x² = 1: R (x) = 3 (1)² - 2x (1) - 5 (1) + 6 = 3 - 2x - 5 + 6 = -2x + 4.

exam_questions.question_text: If log₃ y = x and log₂ z = x, then 72ˣ is equal to:
exam_questions.option_a: y z³
exam_questions.option_b: y² z³
exam_questions.option_c: y³ z²
exam_questions.explanation: From log₃ y = x, we have 3ˣ = y. From log₂ z = x, we have 2ˣ = z. Prime factorize 72 = 9 * 8 = 3² * 2³. Therefore, 72ˣ = (3² * 2³)ˣ = (3ˣ)² * (2ˣ)³ = y² z³.

exam_questions.question_text: What is the domain of the function f (x) = log (1 - x) + √(x² - 1)?
exam_questions.explanation: Condition 1 (logarithm argument): 1 - x > 0 => x < 1. Condition 2 (square root radicand): x² - 1 ≥ 0 => x ≤ -1 or x ≥ 1. Taking the intersection of (-∞, 1) and ((-∞, -1] ∪ [1, ∞)) gives x ∈ (-∞, -1].

exam_questions.question_text: If p (x) is a polynomial of degree m, then which one of the following is always true?
exam_questions.option_a: p (x) is an even function.
exam_questions.option_b: p (x) has m - 1 turning points.
exam_questions.option_c: Its graph is down on the left and up on the right.
exam_questions.option_d: p (x) has at most m zeros.
options: Its graph is down on the left and up on the right.
p(x) has at most m zeros.
exam_questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, a polynomial of degree m has at most m real zeros (roots). Turning points can be fewer than m - 1, parity depends on powers, and end behavior depends on the sign of the leading coefficient.

exam_questions.question_text: If the zeros of polynomial function p (x) are -2 and 0, then the zeros of p (x² - 5x + 4) is equal to____.
exam_questions.option_a: 1, 2 and 3
exam_questions.option_b: 2, 3 and 4
exam_questions.explanation: For p (u) = 0, we must have u = 0 or u = -2. Case 1: x² - 5x + 4 = 0 => (x - 1)(x - 4) = 0 => x = 1, x = 4. Case 2: x² - 5x + 4 = -2 => x² - 5x + 6 = 0 => (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0 => x = 2, x = 3. Therefore, the set of zeros is {1, 2, 3, 4}.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: If (a/b)^(x - 1) = (b/a)^(x - 3), then which of the following is the value of x?
exam_questions.explanation:
Rewrite (b/a)^(x - 3) as ((a/b)⁻¹)^(x - 3) = (a/b)^(-(x - 3)) = (a/b)^(3 - x). Equating the exponents:
x - 1 = 3 - x
2x = 4 => x = 2.

exam_questions.question_text: If log₂ 7 = x, then x is:
exam_questions.option_a: an irrational number such that 2 < x < 3.
exam_questions.option_b: a rational number such that 0 < x < 2.
exam_questions.option_c: a rational number such that 2 < x < 3.
exam_questions.option_d: a prime number of the form 7x + 2
options: an irrational number such that 2 < x < 3.
a rational number such that 0 < x < 2.
a rational number such that 2 < x < 3.
a prime number of the form 7x + 2
exam_questions.explanation: Since 2² = 4 < 7 < 8 = 2³, taking log base 2 gives 2 < log₂ 7 < 3. Because 7 is not a rational power of 2, log₂ 7 cannot be expressed as a ratio of integers and is therefore irrational.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following could be the graph of a polynomial function?

A smooth, continuous wave-like curve with no breaks or sharp corners

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a polynomial?

exam_questions.explanation: A polynomial contains only non-negative integer powers of x and real coefficients. The absolute value function |x - 2| involves piece wise definitions and a sharp corner, making it non-polynomial.

exam_questions.question_text: If -1 and 1 are two real roots of the polynomial function f (x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d and the point (0, 3) is the y-intercept of the graph of f, then which of the following can be the possible value of b?
exam_questions.explanation:
From y-intercept (0, 3): f (0) = d = 3. Since 1 and -1 are roots:
f (1) = a (1)³ + b (1)² + c (1) + 3 = 0 => a + b + c = -3
f(-1) = a(-1)³ + b(-1)² + c(-1) + 3 = 0 => -a + b - c = -3
Adding both equations: (a + b + c) + (-a + b - c) = -3 + (-3) => 2b = -6 => b = -3.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Let a and b be non-zero real numbers, and m and n be positive integers. Which of the following is true?
exam_questions.option_a: (aⁿ)ᵐ = aⁿ⁺ᵐ
exam_questions.option_b: aᵐ · a⁻ⁿ = a⁻ᵐⁿ
exam_questions.option_c: aⁿ / a⁻ᵐ = aⁿ⁺ᵐ
exam_questions.explanation: By law of exponents for quotients: aⁿ / a⁻ᵐ = aⁿ⁻⁽⁻ᵐ⁾ = aⁿ⁺ᵐ.

exam_questions.question_text: If f (x) and g (x) are n and m degree polynomial functions respectively and h (x) is the product of f (x) and g (x), then which one of the following is NOT true about h (x)?

exam_questions.option_b: It has at most n + m roots.
exam_questions.option_c: It has at most n + m - 1 turning points.
exam_questions.option_d: It has at most n + m y-intercepts.
options: It has at most n + m roots.
It has at most n + m - 1 turning points.
It has at most n + m y-intercepts.
exam_questions.explanation: Every single-variable function has at most ONE y-intercept (at x = 0), never n + m y-intercepts.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT true about the graph of the polynomial function f (x) = 2x⁵ - 7x³ + 2x - 1?

exam_questions.option_b: It is a smooth and continuous curve.
exam_questions.option_c: It crosses y-axis at (0, -1).

options: As we move far from the origin, it rises upward to the left and falls down to the right.
It is a smooth and continuous curve.
It has at most 4 turning points and intersects the x-axis at most 5 times.
exam_questions.explanation: The leading term is 2x⁵ (odd degree 5, positive leading coefficient a_n = 2 > 0). The end behavior for odd degree with positive coefficient is: falls to the left (x -> -∞, f (x) -> -∞) and rises to the right (x -> ∞, f (x) -> ∞). Option A asserts the exact opposite, so it is FALSE.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: The solution set of the equation x⁶ + x⁵ - 9x⁴ - 9x³ = 0 is:
exam_questions.explanation:
Factor out x³:
x³(x³ + x² - 9x - 9) = 0
Factor by grouping in the parentheses:
x³[x²(x + 1) - 9 (x + 1)] = 0
x³(x + 1)(x² - 9) = 0
x³(x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3) = 0
Setting each factor to zero gives x = 0, x = -1, x = 3, and x = -3. Solution set = {-3, -1, 0, 3}.

exam_questions.question_text: The expression 4 log a - (1/2) log b + log c is equivalent to:

exam_questions.option_c: log (4ac / √b)
exam_questions.explanation:
Apply power and quotient/product laws of logarithms:
4 log a - (1/2) log b + log c = log (a⁴) - log (b^(1/2)) + log (c) = log (a⁴ · c / √b).

exam_questions.question_text: Let f and g be polynomial functions such that f (x) = x³ - 2x² + 5x + 3 and g (x) = 5x³ + x² + 4, then which one of the following is polynomial function?

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is true about the zero (s) of a function f (x)?

options: If f(c) = 0, then y = c is the y-intercept.

exam_questions.explanation: By the Factor Theorem, a number c is a root/zero of polynomial f (x) (i.e. f (c) = 0) if and only if (x - c) is a factor of f (x).

exam_questions.question_text: When the polynomial function f (x) = 3x⁶ + 5x⁴ + 8x³ - kx² + 10 is divided by x - 1 the remainder is 6. What is the value of k?
exam_questions.explanation:
By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder upon division by (x - 1) equals f (1):
f (1) = 3 (1)⁶ + 5 (1)⁴ + 8 (1)³ - k (1)² + 10 = 6
3 + 5 + 8 - k + 10 = 6
26 - k = 6 => k = 26 - 6 = 20.

exam_questions.question_text: If f: [2, ∞) → ℝ be the function defined by f (x) = x² - 4x + 5, then the range of f (x) is equal to:

exam_questions.explanation: Complete the square: f (x) = (x - 2)² + 1. For x ∈ [2, ∞), (x - 2) ≥ 0, so (x - 2)² takes all values in [0, ∞). Adding 1, f (x) takes all values in [0 + 1, ∞) = [1, ∞).

exam_questions.question_text: If f is a polynomial function given by f (x) = 2x³ + 4x² + 5x - 9, then this function has root between_______.

exam_questions.option_b: 0 and 1

exam_questions.explanation:
Evaluate f (x) at integer values:
f (0) = 2 (0)³ + 4 (0)² + 5 (0) - 9 = -9 < 0
f (1) = 2 (1)³ + 4 (1)² + 5 (1) - 9 = 2 + 4 + 5 - 9 = 2 > 0
Since f (0) < 0 and f (1) > 0, by the Intermediate Value Theorem there exists a root in the interval (0, 1).

exam_questions.question_text: For a positive real number b ≠ 1, suppose log_b (x - y) = 2, log_b (x + y) = 4 and log_b y = 2. Then which of the following is NOT true?
exam_questions.option_a: x = 2b²
exam_questions.option_c: log_b (x/y) = log_b 2
exam_questions.explanation:
From given equations:
(x - y) = b²
(x + y) = b⁴
y = b² => x = y + b² = 2b². Now evaluate D: (x⁴ - y⁴)/(x² + y²) = x² - y² = (x - y)(x + y).
log_b ((x⁴ - y⁴)/(x² + y²)) = log_b ((x - y)(x + y)) = log_b (x - y) + log_b (x + y) = 2 + 4 = 6 ≠ 8. Thus D is false.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following graphs is possible represent ation of the exponential functions y = 3ˣ and y = 5ˣ?

exam_questions.question_text: Given log 5 = b, then log₅ 4 is equal to:

log₅ 4 = log 4 / log 5 = (2 log 2) / log 5 = 2 (1 - b) / b = 2 (1/b - 1).

exam_questions.question_text: Let f (x) = (3/4)ˣ and g (x) = (4/3)ˣ. Which one of the following statements about f (x) and g (x) is true?

exam_questions.option_c: If x < 0, then g (x) < 1 and if x > 0, then f (x) < 1

If x < 0, then g(x) < 1 and if x > 0, then f(x) < 1
exam_questions.explanation: Since 0 < 3/4 < 1, f (x) is strictly decreasing: for x > 0, f (x) < (3/4)⁰ = 1. Since 4/3 > 1, g (x) is strictly increasing: for x < 0, g (x) < (4/3)⁰ = 1. Therefore, option C correctly states both facts.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a polynomial function f (x) of degree 4 such that the zeros of f are -3, -1, 0, 2 and f (3) = 288?
exam_questions.option_a: f (x) = x⁴ + 2x³ - 5x² - 6x
exam_questions.option_b: f (x) = 4x⁴ + 8x³ - 20x² - 24x
exam_questions.option_c: f (x) = 4x⁴ + 2x³ - 5x² - 6x
exam_questions.explanation:
Set up the polynomial in factored form: f (x) = a x (x + 3)(x + 1)(x - 2). Substitute x = 3:
f (3) = a (3)(3 + 3)(3 + 1)(3 - 2) = a (3)(6)(4)(1) = 72a = 288 => a = 4. Expand:
f (x) = 4x[(x + 3)(x + 1)(x - 2)] = 4x (x³ + 2x² - 5x - 6) = 4x⁴ + 8x³ - 20x² - 24x.

exam_questions.question_text: If f (x) = 2x⁴ - 3x³ + 5x² - x + 1 and g (x) = 3x³ + x - 2, then which of the following is NOT true about f and g?

exam_questions.question_text: If the polynomial functions g (x) = x² + 4, q (x) = x - 3 and r (x) = 3x + 2, and a function f (x) is given by f (x)/g (x) = q (x) + r (x)/g (x), then which one of the following is NOT true about f (x)?

Multiply through by g (x):

= x³ - 3x² + 4x - 12 + 3x + 2 = x³ - 3x² + 7x - 10. Option D asserts f (x) = x³ + 3x² - 7x + 10 (with inverted signs), which is FALSE.

exam_questions.question_text: If x + 1 is a common factor of the expressions x² + (a - b) x and 3x² - (a + 2) x - (a + 5b), then find the value of a + b.
exam_questions.explanation:
Substitute x = -1 into both expressions:
Expression 1: (-1)² + (a - b)(-1) = 0 => 1 - a + b = 0 => a - b = 1 --- (1) Expression 2: 3(-1)² - (a + 2)(-1) - (a + 5b) = 0 => 3 + a + 2 - a - 5b = 0 => 5 - 5b = 0 => b = 1. From (1): a = 1 + b = 1 + 1 = 2. Then a + b = 2 + 1 = 3.

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an onto function?
exam_questions.option_a: f : ℝ → ℝ is defined by f (x) = x² + 5x + 6.
exam_questions.option_b: f : ℝ → ℝ is defined by f (x) = |3x + 4| + 2.

exam_questions.option_d: f : ℝ → [5, ∞) is defined by f (x) = x² + 5.
options: f : ℝ → ℝ is defined by f(x) = x² + 5x + 6.
f : ℝ → ℝ is defined by f(x) = |3x + 4| + 2.
f : ℝ → (0, ∞) is defined by f(x) = x².
f : ℝ → [5, ∞) is defined by f(x) = x² + 5.
exam_questions.explanation: A function is onto (surjective) if its range equals its codomain. For f (x) = x² + 5 with domain ℝ, x² ∈ [0, ∞), so f (x) ∈ [5, ∞), which matches the codomain [5, ∞) exactly.
exam_questions.section_instruction: Choose the best answer from the given alternatives.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true?

exam_questions.question_text: From the given graphs, which one can represent the graph of f (x) = x³ + 3x² - x - 3?

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT a reason why carbon forms a uniquely vast number of organic compounds?

exam_questions.question_text: In which of the following hydrocarbons are all the carbon atoms sp-hybridized?
exam_questions.option_a: Ethene

exam_questions.option_c: Propene
exam_questions.explanation: Ethyne (acetylene, H-C≡C-H) has a carbon-carbon triple bond where each carbon forms two sigma bonds (one with H and one with C) and two pi bonds, requiring sp hybridization for both carbon atoms.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the physical properties of alkanes?

exam_questions.question_text: Which pair of organic compounds belongs to the same homologous series?

exam_questions.option_c: C3H8 and C4H10

exam_questions.question_text: Which one of the following carbon-containing compounds is classified as an INORGANIC compound?

exam_questions.question_text: In saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), the geometry around each carbon atom is:

exam_questions.question_text: A hydrocarbon is described as 'saturated' because:

exam_questions.question_text: The chlorination of methane in the presence of ultraviolet (UV) light proceeds via which mechanism?

exam_questions.question_text: According to Markovnikov’s rule, when an unsymmetrical hydrogen halide (HX) adds across the double bond of an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen atom attaches to:

exam_questions.option_b: The double-bonded carbon bearing fewer hydrogen atoms.
exam_questions.option_c: Either carbon atom with equal probability.
options: The double-bonded carbon bearing the greater number of hydrogen atoms.
The double-bonded carbon bearing fewer hydrogen atoms.
Either carbon atom with equal probability.
exam_questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule states that in the electrophilic addition of an unsymmetrical reagent (HX) to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen ion (electrophile) adds to the carbon with more attached hydrogen atoms to yield the more stable carbocation intermediate.

exam_questions.question_text: The reaction of an alkene with cold, alkaline potassium permanganate solution (Baeyer’s reagent) produces:

exam_questions.option_c: Alkane
exam_questions.explanation: Baeyer's reagent (cold, dilute, alkaline KMnO4) oxidizes alkenes by syn-dihydroxylation to form vicinal diols (1,2-diols or glycols), with the purple permanganate decolourising to form a brown MnO2 precipitate.

exam_questions.question_text: When bromine water (Br2 in CCl4) is shaken with an alkene (such as ethene), what visual change is observed?

exam_questions.option_b: A dense white precipitate forms.
exam_questions.option_c: The solution turns intensely purple.
exam_questions.option_d: Bubbles of hydrogen gas are evolved.
options: The reddish-brown color of bromine is decolourized immediately.
Bubbles of hydrogen gas are evolved.
exam_questions.explanation: Bromine adds rapidly across the carbon-carbon double bond forming a colourless 1,2-dibromoalkane, causing the characteristic reddish-brown bromine solution to discharge (decolourise), which serves as a diagnostic test for unsaturation.

exam_questions.question_text: The characteristic chemical reactions of alkenes are primarily:

exam_questions.question_text: What is the IUPAC name for the alkene CH3-CH=CH-CH (CH3)-CH3?

exam_questions.question_text: The general molecular formula for aliphatic acyclic alkynes is:

exam_questions.option_c: CnH2n

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following alkynes will form a precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens’ reagent)?

exam_questions.option_b: 1-Butyne (CH3-CH2-C≡C-H)

exam_questions.explanation: Terminal alkynes (like 1-butyne) contain a weakly acidic sp-hybridized C-H hydrogen atom that reacts with ammoniacal silver nitrate to form a heavy, insoluble white precipitate of silver alkynide (CH3-CH2-C≡C-Ag). exam_questions.question_text: Hydrogenation of an alkyne using hydrogen gas in the presence of Lindlar’s catalyst (palladium poisoned with CaCO3 and quinoline) yields:

exam_questions.question_text: Hydration of ethyne (acetylene) by passing it into warm dilute H2SO4 in the presence of HgSO4 catalyst yields which final carbonyl product?

exam_questions.question_text: The functional group characteristic of aliphatic alcohols is the:

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds is an example of a tertiary (3°) alcohol?

exam_questions.question_text: Dehydration of ethanol with excess concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4) at 170 °C produces:

exam_questions.question_text: The Lucas reagent, used to differentiate between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols, consists of a mixture of:

exam_questions.question_text: Phenol (C6H5OH) is more acidic than aliphatic alcohols (such as ethanol) because:
