exam_questions.section_instruction: Reading Passage II: Child Abuse
exam_questions.reading_passage: Child abuse is a phenomenon that knows no social, geographic or racial boundaries. It occurs in the best of families in wealthy suburbs and in rural areas as well. It is, in fact, a national plague that experts say is likely to create another generation of child abusers in America from among those being abused today. For years, the problem was hidden behind the closed doors of houses or apartments. But, since the passage of laws in the 1970s requiring health and social professionals to report all cases of suspected abuse, a quiet revolution has been occur ring. More cases of child abuse are being reported, and social welfare agencies are getting help for both the children and their parents. That is not to say, however, that the reporting is in any way complete. More than 5,000 cases are reported annually to the Philadelphia County Children and Youth Agency, but a spokes woman said, " There's a lot more out there that goes unreported. Schools are just now beginning to focus on abuse," the spokes woman said. " Out of the quarter-million kids within the Philadelphia schools, we received only 300 reports last year. However, the schools are making strides in this area," she said. To increase the frequency of reporting, institutions that come into contact with injured children are training staff members to recognize abuse. The tremendous amount of stress in today's society both within and outside the home is considered one of the main factors in the rise of child abuse. Poor marital relationships, single parenthood, social and economic problems, unemployment and social isolation add undue stress to our lives. The problem of social isolation is critical. Today, people are moving around and finding themselves living further away from their families and the emotional support which they provide. Mothers find themselves living either in large city apartment complexes or suburban communities in which they know absolutely no one. In this lonely atmosphere, they try to deal with the pressures of being the parent of one, two or three children.
exam_questions.option_a: Child abuse should not be practiced.
exam_questions.option_b: Child abuse is everywhere regardless.
exam_questions.option_c: Whether young or old, you are always abused.
exam_questions.option_d: Some races in the world do not practice child abuse.

exam_questions.question_text: Aluminum metal reacts spontaneously with iron (II) ions according to the reaction: $$2\text{Al}(s) + 3\text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) \right arrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(aq) + 3\text{Fe}(s)$$ What is the value of $\Delta G^\circ$ for the reaction?
exam_questions.option_b: $-608\text{ kJ}$
exam_questions.option_c: $-706\text{ kJ}$
exam_questions.explanation: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = -0.44\text{ V} - (-1.66\text{ V}) = +1.22\text{ V}$. For $n = 6\text{ mol } e^-$: $$\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ = -6 \times 96500\text{ C/mol} \times 1.22\text{ V} = -706380\text{ J} = -706.4\text{ kJ} \approx -706\text{ kJ}$$

exam_questions.question_text: What is the molar mass of a polyethylene sample, $[-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-]_n$, when $n = 4600$?

| \text{D} | \text{are generally recyclable} | \text{Can't be recyclable} |

$$

exam_questions.question_text: For the electrolysis of aqueous copper (II) sulfate solution using graphite electrode, what substances produced at anode and cathode electrode respectively and their ratio?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{Cu}$ and $\text{O}_2$ are produced in a mol ratio of $2:1$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ are produced in a mol ratio of $1:1$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ are produced in a mol ratio of $2:1$
exam_questions.option_d: $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{Cu}$ are produced in a mol ratio of $1:2$
exam_questions.explanation: At the anode, water oxidizes: $2\text{H}_2\text{O} \right arrow \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4e^-$ ($1\text{ mol } \text{O}_2 / 4e^-$). At the cathode, copper reduces: $2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4e^- \right arrow 2\text{Cu}$ ($2\text{ mol } \text{Cu} / 4e^-$). Hence, $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{Cu}$ are generated in a $1:2$ molar ratio.

exam_questions.explanation: Aerobic cellular respiration combusts glucose with oxygen to yield carbon dioxide, water, and ATP energy: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + 6\text{O}_2 \right arrow 6\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Energy}$.

exam_questions.question_text: The following gases are contributed to the green house effect on Earth. Which is the correct order of their importance from greatest to smallest in the natural green house effect?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{CO}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{CH}_4$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{CO}_2, \text{CH}_4$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{CH}_4, \text{CO}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}$
exam_questions.explanation: In Earth's atmosphere, water vapor ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) contributes roughly $36-70\%$ of the green house effect, followed by carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$, $9-26\%$) and methane ($\text{CH}_4$, $4-9\%$).

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following sample routine correctly indicate the extraction of copper from is principal-ore?
exam_questions.option_a: $\text{Concentration of ores} \Right arrow \text{Reduction} \Right arrow \text{Roasting} \Right arrow \text{Purification}$
exam_questions.option_b: $\text{Concentration of ores} \Right arrow \text{Purification} \Right arrow \text{Roasting} \Right arrow \text{Reduction}$
exam_questions.option_c: $\text{Purification} \Right arrow \text{Concentration of ores} \Right arrow \text{Reduction} \Right arrow \text{Roasting}$
exam_questions.explanation: Metallurgical extraction of copper proceeds sequentially: 1) Froth flotation concentration, 2) Roasting sulfide ore in air, 3) Smelting reduction to blister copper, 4) Electrolytic refining purification.

exam_questions.question_text: Which of the following is TRUE about a homologous series?
exam_questions.option_a: A group of compounds with different functional group
exam_questions.option_b: A group of isomers with the same boiling point
exam_questions.option_c: Compounds with different molecular masses but the same formula
exam_questions.option_d: hydrocarbons where each member differs from the next by a repeating unit $-\text{CH}_2-$
exam_questions.explanation: A homologous series is a series of organic compounds possessing the same general formula and functional group, in which each successive member differs from the previous one by a methylene ($-\text{CH}_2-$) unit.

exam_questions.question_text:
The following reaction can be used for the synthesis of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$ as a desired product:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{S}^- \long right arrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{SH} + \text{Br}^-$$
What is the atom economy for the above reaction?
exam_questions.explanation: Atom economy is given by: $$\text{Atom Economy} = \frac{\text{Molar mass of desired product}}{\text{Total molar mass of all reactants}} \times 100\%$$ Desired product $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8 = 4 (12.0) + 8 (1.0) = 56.0\text{ g/mol}$. Reactants: $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br} (136.9) + \text{CH}_3\text{S}^- (47.1) = 184.0\text{ g/mol}$. $$\text{Atom Economy} = \frac{56.0}{184.0} \times 100\% = 30.43\% \approx 30.4\%$$
